SP Gel/DS@cLip demonstrated favorable injectability, self-healing capacity, lubrication performance and biocompatibility. Notably, the hydrogel system enables rapid SP release to target early synovial inflammation and sustained DS release to inhibit chondrocyte pyroptosis, exerting significant cartilage protective effects both in vitro and in vivo. This pathological progression features-guided biphasic drug delivery system offers a promising therapeutic approach with strong potential for clinical translation in OA treatment.

articles.title: Biphasic dysregulation of non-muscle myosin IIA drives the AKI-to-CKD transition via an ALDH1A1-retinoic acid-HBEGF/EGFR signaling axis in tubular cells.
articles.abstract: The decision between successful repair and pathological fibrosis following kidney injury remains a pivotal yet poorly understood process. Here, we identify non-muscle myosin IIA (NM IIA) as a master regulator of renal tubular fate whose biphasic dysregulation dictates the transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Using integrated single-cell transcriptomics and multi-model validation, we define this dysregulation as stage-dependent alterations in NM IIA expression and subcellular localization: it is downregulated in AKI, impairing regenerative repair, but pathologically overexpressed and aberrantly localized to the nucleus in CKD, where it drives maladaptive fibrosis. Mechanistically, upon nuclear translocation in tubular epithelial cells, NM IIA directly transactivates Aldh1a1, thereby enhancing local retinoic acid (RA) biosynthesis. This RA signal subsequently propagates through HBEGF/EGFR signaling to influence repair outcomes. Collectively, our work delineates an NM IIA/ALDH1A1-RA-HBEGF/EGFR axis, revealing how NM IIA, beyond its cytoskeletal function, acts as a transcriptional regulator that integrates mechanical and metabolic cues in the kidney. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for the AKI-to-CKD transition and highlight potential stage-specific therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Engineered αvβ6-targeting peptide‒BSH conjugates for boron neutron capture therapy of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by a dense stroma that impedes drug penetration and establishes an immune-"cold" microenvironment. Conventional external beam radiotherapy is often limited by off-target toxicity to surrounding normal tissues due to the complex anatomy of the pancreas. Boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) is a binary targeted radiotherapy that utilizes a focused thermal neutron beam to trigger the in situ production of high-energy particles, enabling single-cell-scale tumor cell ablation. However, the efficacy of BNCT in PDAC critically depends on the ability of B-10 carriers to effectively penetrate the dense stromal barrier and achieve efficient internalization into tumor cells. Herein, we developed nine αvβ6 integrin-targeting peptide‒BSH conjugates to optimize the BNCT therapeutic index. By optimizing linker structure and the number of BSH moieties, amphiphilic agents with enhanced PDAC cellular uptake were obtained. The lead compound, namely DOTA-2BB, adopts a "trident-shaped" structure that facilitates stromal penetration and exhibits the optimal tumor uptake and retention. In a PDAC mouse model, administration of DOTA-2BB followed by thermal neutron irradiation resulted in suppression of tumor growth with favorable biosafety. These findings establish DOTA-2BB as a promising B-10 carrier for PDAC and provide a strategy for treating stroma-rich tumors.

articles.title: Nursing interventions for managing treatment-related adverse effects of targeted anti-tumor therapies in adult cancer patients: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Targeted anti-tumor therapies, including tyrosine kinase inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates, and immune checkpoint inhibitors, have improved clinical outcomes and survival across multiple cancers but are associated with clinically significant dermatologic, neurological, gastrointestinal, hematologic, and immune-related toxicities that compromise adherence and quality of life. OBJECTIVES: This scoping review aimed to systematically map the available evidence on nursing interventions used to prevent, monitor, and manage adverse effects associated with targeted anti-tumor therapies in adult cancer patients. METHODS: Eligible studies were English-language publications conducted between 2015 and 2025 that focused on nurse-led or nursing-centered interventions addressing the adverse effects of targeted anti-tumor therapies in adult oncology populations. Data were charted using a standardized form and synthesized descriptively by intervention type and adverse-effect domain. RESULTS: Of 742 records identified, 14 studies met the inclusion criteria. Study designs included two quasi-experimental studies and one randomized controlled trial protocol two cohort studies, seven narrative or integrative reviews, and two clinical practice guidelines. Five principal intervention categories were identified: patient education and self-management support; nurse-led oral targeted-drug management and continuity-of-care programs; home-based multidisciplinary interventions; telephone and telehealth-based toxicity monitoring; and symptom-specific supportive-care strategies. Across diverse settings, structured nursing interventions reduced toxicity burden, improved medication adherence, decreased unplanned healthcare use, and enhanced patient-reported quality of life and psychosocial outcomes. CONCLUSION: Nurse-led interventions may have an important and promising role in supporting the safe and effective use of targeted anti-tumor therapies in adults with cancer. Integrating structured education, continuity of care, multidisciplinary collaboration, and telehealth-enabled monitoring into routine oncology practice may optimize toxicity management and support treatment adherence. Further multicenter trials are needed to evaluate nursing protocols for antibody-drug conjugate-induced neuropathy and immune-related adverse events and to examine long-term clinical and economic outcomes. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://osf.io/5nvfe/identifier, 5nvfe.

articles.title: A systematic review on the possible role of microRNA-155 in cancer treatment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Overexpression of microRNA-155 (miR-155) has been associated with cancer development, metastasis, and possible drug resistance. This systematic review analyzed the evidence from the existing literature on miR-155 expression in cancer patients undergoing treatment. METHODS: A thorough literature search was conducted in databases and search engines (ProQuest, PubMed, and Google Scholar) from January 2019 to December 2024 to identify clinical evidence on miR-155 expression in cancer treatments. To assess miR-155 expression in relation to clinical outcomes, we included 15 cancers in this systematic review. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, three independent reviewers selected, extracted, and assessed the data against the predefined inclusion criteria, and a fourth reviewer verified the assessments and resolved discrepancies. RESULTS: Of the 15 cancers analyzed, 19 eligible studies covering eight cancers were identified and included in the review, namely breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia, cutaneous melanoma, non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, papillary thyroid cancer, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Screening and evaluation of these 19 studies showed that miR-155 expression varied by cancer type, treatment strategy, and patient sample type. While most studies associated miR-155 overexpression with treatment resistance, a few reported an association between elevated miR-155 expression and enhanced treatment sensitivity. A limitation of this study is that the search for studies reporting miR-155 expression in relation to therapeutic outcomes in patients with cancer was restricted to three databases and a 5-year timeframe. CONCLUSION: Overall, the results of this study indicate that the prognostic and predictive significance of miR-155 warrants further evaluation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO ID, CRD42025632573.

articles.title: FDA approves plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy for rare viral disease.
Designing chemical linkage for boosting combination photo-immunotherapy.
Beyond M1/M2 dichotomy: Toward an operationally defined, modular framework for macrophage functional states.
articles.abstract: Macrophages are versatile immune cells involved in tissue homeostasis, host defense, inflammation, and disease progression. Their biology has traditionally been interpreted through the M1/M2 paradigm, but single-cell and spatial profiling, lineage tracing, and multi-omics reveal substantially greater heterogeneity. This review organizes macrophage diversity around recurring functional programs: immunosuppressive/regulatory, matrix-remodeling, hypoxia-associated metabolic, IFN-responsive/antigen-presenting, and proliferative. Angiogenic/perivascular activity is treated as a putative program because its status as a distinct transcriptional entity remains uncertain. We introduce an operational framework based on three criteria-co-expression coherence, combinatorial independence, and microenvironmental inducibility-to distinguish candidate functional modules from broader programs. We also conduct an evidence-weighted assessment of these programs, examining their independent variation, contextual coupling, and co-occurrence. Furthermore, we propose a Macrophage Dominance Index (MDI) as a hypothesis-generating numerical framework, with provisional marker sets, weighting, and formula requiring independent validation. Finally, we derive falsifiable predictions and outline experimental, single-cell, spatial, and clinical strategies to test relationships among programs. Overall, available evidence suggests substantial coupling among macrophage functional programs rather than uniformly independent functional axes. Macrophage heterogeneity is therefore better understood as context-dependent combinations of programs, some of which remain unconfirmed as distinct transcriptional modules. Although the framework may inform macrophage biology broadly, most supporting evidence, particularly concerning program relationships, biomarkers, prognosis, and therapeutic implications, derives from tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). Its applicability to non-cancer settings remains to be established. The MDI and proposed predictions are intended to facilitate testable research, not to serve as validated diagnostic, prognostic, or therapeutic tools.

articles.title: Engineered dendritic cell-derived extracellular vesicles: novel vaccines in cancer immunotherapy, Challenges and perspectives.
articles.abstract: Dendritic cells (DCs) are the most well-known immune cells for cancer immunotherapy progress. The engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) from DCs (DCs-EVs) for immunotherapy have emerged as a novel and effective therapeutic approach because they naturally contribute to regulating immune responses by transporting therapeutic agents to target cells with minimal toxicity and high specificity. DCs-EVs, are heterogeneous extracellular particles, generally contribute to intracellular communication and immune regulation due to the presence of immune-regulatory molecules, antigens, major histocompatibility complexes, and co-stimulatory molecules. As a result, engineered DCs-EVs are defined as lipid bilayer delimited EVs released by DCs that have been intentionally pre- or post-isolated to change their surface composition, cargo, targeting properties, biodistribution, or immunomodulatory function. DCs-EVs have been examined for breast cancer, colorectal cancer, melanoma, and glioblastoma. Although engineered DCs-EVs have demonstrated hopeful results in preclinical experiments, for clinical translation, some limitations remain to be addressed in further studies. In addition, for clinical trials, these EVs must comply with good manufacturing practice (GMP). This narrative review was informed by a structured literature search about the application of engineered DCs-EVs in cancer immunotherapy utilizing sources like Google Scholar, Scopus, ScienceDirect, PubMed, and WOS. Furthermore, it discussed EVs biology, engineering methods, and clinical trials, as well as outlined challenges and perspectives in this field.

articles.title: Migraine in mitochondrial diseases and disorders: a bioenergetic perspective.
articles.abstract: Migraine is a neurological disorder increasingly recognized as involving systemic and neuronal bioenergetic vulnerability - a state marked by cellular energy disruption, impaired mitochondrial function, and reduced ATP-generating capacity. Accumulating evidence implicates mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired oxidative phosphorylation as contributors to migraine pathophysiology, linking cellular energy deficits to cortical spreading depression, trigeminovascular activation, and oxidative stress. These pathophysiological mechanisms and related channelopathies shape the cellular energetic landscape. Under these conditions, metabolic disturbances influence symptom variability and phenotype heterogeneity, although the directionality of these relationships reflects a dynamic, bidirectional feedback loop between bioenergetic stress and migraine pathobiology. Here, we describe mechanisms by which limited energetic reserve modulates migraine onset, symptom evolution, and recovery. We review phase-specific bioenergetic shifts across the migraine cycle and highlight how these core cellular processes modulate network excitability. In parallel, we summarize key biomarkers, including calcitonin gene-related peptide and growth differentiation factor 15, together with related salivary or oral-fluid assays, which assist in multi-compartment biological profiling. This pathobiological axis interfaces with localized molecular signaling cascades, including pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide signaling, sirtuin biology, microRNA-based and epigenetic regulation, and gene-informed mechanisms. This progression underscores a growing interest in molecular pathways governing neuronal energy balance and in exploratory metabolic and mitochondrial-supportive compounds. Together, these observations offer a mechanistic overview of migraine as a disorder where metabolic homeostasis affects expression, severity, and recovery - a framework that may inform future biomarker research and mechanistically targeted interventions, particularly in individuals with primary mitochondrial disease.

articles.title: Factors influencing interactions between protein-containing drug solutions and containers: A structured, critical review.
articles.abstract: During manufacturing, storage, and delivery, therapeutic proteins can interact with their containers. Protein adsorption to surfaces is a complex process that may or may not be reversible but can lead to total or partial unfolding of the adsorbed protein or, in contrast, to minimal disturbances in the protein's structure. The objective of the present study was to review the literature data on factors influencing interactions between proteins in ready-to-inject drug solutions and their containers. The MEDLINE, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar databases were searched with various keyword-based queries. Studies included in the review had to specify the type of container (e.g., a bag or a syringe), the container material (e.g., polyvinylchloride or glass), and container extractables (e.g., silicone oil). Protein-related factors were also considered, including the type of protein, its concentration, and the presence of excipients (e.g., polysorbate (PS) or poloxamer surfactants). A total of 451 records were screened, and 26 articles were ultimately included in the review. Thirteen articles focused on the container's type and material composition, eight other articles addressed the presence of silicone oil in the container, and five other articles explored the impact of excipients on protein-container interactions. The main factors influencing protein-container interactions were the container material, formulation additives, and physical processing. The effects of these factors were, however, strongly system-dependent and not uniform: the same factor, a surfactant, NaCl, sucrose, or silicone oil, could either mitigate or promote adsorption and particle formation, depending on the protein, the formulation, and the interface involved. Rather than being universal, the factors influence the balance between each molecule's conformational and colloidal stability and must therefore be assessed case by case. Controlling these factors during storage, handling, and administration is essential for preserving the quality of the administered compound.

articles.title: Vicatia thibetica H. Boissieu: An ethnopharmacological review of botany, phytochemistry, traditional uses, pharmacological activities, safety, quality control, and applications.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The dried root of Vicatia thibetica H. Boissieu (VTR) is an ethnomedicinal and medicinal-food resource traditionally used in Tibetan medicine, Bai folk medicine, and regional dietary practices in southwestern China. Traditionally, VTR has been used as a tonic and dietary medicine for relieving fatigue, regulating menstruation, and alleviating gastrointestinal and cold-dampness-related disorders. Despite its long history of use and potential applications in functional foods and traditional compound preparations, current evidence regarding its active constituents, pharmacological mechanisms, quality control strategies, and safety remains incomplete and requires systematic validation. AIM OF THE WORK: This review aims to critically evaluate the ethnopharmacological evidence supporting the traditional use and rational development of VTR. By integrating Tibetan medical records, Bai folk medicinal practices, regional materia medica, modern dietary uses, phytochemical reports, pharmacological studies, safety data, quality-control evidence, and patent-based applications, this review focuses on the source traceability of traditional uses, the distinction between the botanical species and the medicinal material, the reliability of chemical identification, the evidence level of pharmacological findings, and the major gaps that currently limit quality standardization, safety evaluation, and product development of VTR. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comprehensive literature survey on VTR was conducted to collect and evaluate traditional uses, botany, phytochemistry, pharmacological activities, toxicity and safety evaluation, quality control, and patent-based applications. Relevant studies and application-related records were retrieved from major international and Chinese databases and academic search platforms, including Web of Science, PubMed, Google Scholar, SciFinder, X-MOL, Baidu Scholar, CNKI, and Wanfang Data, covering records available from database inception to June 18, 2026. Patent information was retrieved from the China Patent Retrieval System (CPRS) and the CNKI patent database. Searches were performed using Boolean operators (AND/OR) with core plant and medicinal material terms, including "Vicatia thibetica", "Vicatia thibetica H. Boissieu", "Vicatia thibetica de Boiss.", "Xigui", "Jiawa", "Saigui", "" and "", combined with topic terms such as "traditional use", "ethnopharmacology", "Tibetan medicine", "Bai medicine", "botany", "phytochemistry", "chemical constituent", "pharmacology", "toxicity", "safety evaluation", "quality control", "patent", "functional food", and "product development". Records written in English or Chinese, as well as Chinese translations or annotated editions of classical Tibetan medical texts, were considered. Classical Tibetan medical texts, regional materia medica, Bai medicinal monographs, local chronicles, dissertations, and reference lists were additionally consulted to corroborate botanical features, traditional indications, and application-related information. Duplicate records, conference abstracts, editorials, studies unrelated to VTR, reports on other species without clear attribution to V. thibetica, records with low relevance, records for which the full text or complete information was unavailable, reports with insufficient or non-extractable information, records only incidentally mentioning VTR, and patents or formulas in which the role of VTR could not be clearly determined were excluded. Finally, 63 records, including journal articles, dissertations, monographs, local chronicles, and patent records, were included in this review. The literature selection process is shown in Figure 1. Chemical structures were drawn using ChemDraw, and schematic illustrations were prepared using Microsoft PowerPoint. RESULTS: Ethnopharmacological evidence indicates that VTR has long been used in Tibetan and Bai medicine as a tonic and medicinal food for fatigue relief, menstrual regulation, and cold-related disorders. Modern studies suggest potential anti-fatigue, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and gastrointestinal regulatory effects; however, current evidence remains largely based on crude extracts and experimental models, with limited validation of active compounds and molecular mechanisms. Phytochemical studies have identified several classes of constituents, including coumarins, phenylpropanoids, flavonoids, sterols, and polysaccharides, but their contribution to bioactivity remains insufficiently clarified. Quality standardization, safety evaluation, and product development remain major challenges for the rational utilization of VTR. CONCLUSIONS: V. thibetica is an alpine medicinal-food resource with important ethnopharmacological value and potential for further investigation. However, current research remains limited by insufficient phytochemical characterization, unclear structure-activity relationships, inadequate mechanistic investigations, and the lack of standardized quality evaluation systems. Further studies are needed to clarify its chemical basis, active constituents, pharmacological effects, quality standards, safety profile, and sustainable resource utilization, thereby promoting its scientific evaluation, standardization, and sustainable development.

articles.title: Multidimensional regulation of the cytochrome P450 metabolic network in pulmonary arterial hypertension: Homeostatic imbalance, pathological drivers, and environmental interactions.
articles.abstract: The cytochrome P450 superfamily represents a key metabolic regulatory node in the pathophysiology of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Dysregulation of its homeostatic network directly drives disease progression. This review systematically delineates 3 core axes via which the CYP metabolic network modulates PAH pathogenesis. These axes include functional impairment of the protective CYP2C/J-epoxyeicosatrienoic acid axis, aberrant activation of the deleterious CYP4A/F-20-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid axis, and sustained overactivation of the environmental responsive aryl hydrocarbon receptor/CYP1 axis. This article provides an in-depth analysis of the molecular mechanisms, crosstalk, and synergistic pathogenic effects of these 3 axes, which collectively drive pulmonary vasoconstriction, vascular remodeling, and inflammatory cascades in PAH. These 3 factors form a positive feedback vicious cycle through oxidative stress and substrate competition, synergistically promoting pulmonary vasoconstriction, vascular remodeling, and inflammatory cascades, while smoking, obesity, sex hormones, and immune cells mediate differences in pathogenic patterns across populations. Additionally, this review summarizes 3 classes of targeted agents-soluble epoxide hydrolase inhibitors, CYP4 inhibitors, and CYP1A1 inhibitors-and comprehensively evaluates their translational potential, clinical limitations, and optimization strategies such as lung-targeted delivery. Furthermore, the clinical value of metabolic biomarkers, including the epoxyeicosatrienoic acids/dihydroxyeicosatrienoic acids ratio and plasma 20-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid, for PAH subtyping and prognostic assessment is discussed. This review aimed to provide an integrated theoretical framework for elucidating the metabolic etiology of PAH and advancing the development of precision therapies. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Imbalanced cytochrome P450 metabolic networks play a critical role in pulmonary arterial hypertension progression, however, systematic integration of crosstalk among multiple relevant pathways remains lacking. This review delineates 3 interconnected cytochrome P450-dependent pathogenic axes, explaining patient-specific disease patterns and supporting advances in metabolic biomarkers and precision therapeutic strategies for pulmonary arterial hypertension.

articles.title: Augmented cardiac growth hormone signaling in circadian-disrupted cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Circadian disruption, including rotating shift work, social jet lag, and chronic sleep disturbance, is associated with increased cardiovascular risk and may promote cardiac remodeling. The molecular mechanisms connecting clock disruption to structural heart disease remain incompletely defined. This minireview advances the hypothesis that the growth hormone, GH, axis is an underrecognized endocrine mediator. GH secretion is time dependent, with most daily secretion occurring during early nocturnal sleep-in humans. Cardiomyocytes express GH receptors, and GH can activate Janus kinase 2, signal transducer and activator of transcription 5, phosphoinositide 3 kinase and Akt, and mitogen activated protein kinase and extracellular signal regulated kinase pathways that influence cardiac growth and metabolism. We propose that the cardiomyocyte molecular clock restricts GH responsiveness to circadian phases. REV ERBα is a plausible component of this restraint, but direct cardiomyocyte evidence is lacking. Circadian disruption may increase or mistime myocardial GH signaling, promoting hypertrophy, fibrosis, and metabolic inflexibility. The strongest support comes from cardiomyocyte specific Bmal1 deficient mice, which show increased GH induced cardiac STAT5 phosphorylation, increased cardiac Igf1 expression, and remodeling. Reduction of GH receptor gene dosage partially attenuates this phenotype, supporting a causal contribution of cardiac GH signaling. Nevertheless, genetic clock ablation is not equivalent to environmental circadian misalignment in shift work or chronic sleep disruption. We critically evaluate the components of this proposed clock-GH-heart axis, identify unresolved questions, and outline experiments and chronopharmacological strategies to test whether restoring temporal control of GH signaling can prevent pathological remodeling while preserving physiological GH action.

articles.title: Pharmacological reprogramming of myeloid suppression in solid tumors: mechanisms, evidence standards for immune conversion, and biomarker-informed combinations.
articles.abstract: Myeloid cells regulate immune exclusion, T-cell dysfunction, angiogenesis, stromal remodeling, and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in solid tumors. Pharmacological development has moved from nonspecific depletion toward recruitment or survival blockade, intracellular state reprogramming, restoration of antigen presentation, and tumor-selective phagocytosis. Clinical experience nevertheless shows a recurrent gap between biological activity and attributable therapeutic immune conversion. We introduce the Myeloid Immune Conversion Audit Trail (MICAT), a fixed four-level extension of the pharmacological audit trail that grades intratumoral target engagement, conversion of the intended myeloid state, propagation through the immune ecosystem, and randomized clinical attribution. Each level is scored as not demonstrated, partial, or demonstrated. Applying MICAT across representative trials shows that most programs stop at systemic pharmacodynamics or partial lineage effects; few establish ecosystem propagation, and none yet completes the entire causal chain for an immunological switch in a solid-tumor carcinoma. The analysis identifies compensation and redundancy as the central biological obstacle: CCR2 blockade can recruit CXCR2-positive neutrophils, CSF1R inhibition can spare resistant SPP1-high macrophages, and CD40 or PI3Kγ activation can induce interferon-linked PD-L1 feedback. We therefore prioritize lineage-resolved paired tissue, preservation of cDC1 and cDC2 function, absolute cell quantification, orthogonal functional and spatial readouts, and randomized component-controlled trials. Disease context is decisive: tenosynovial giant-cell tumor establishes CSF1R dependence without proving immune conversion; macrophage-rich triple-negative breast cancer is a rational PI3Kγ test-bed; pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma permits sequence-aware CD40 and stromal studies; and microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer is a stringent failure benchmark. CAR-macrophages, in vivo mRNA/lipid-nanoparticle reprogramming, myeloid engagers, and artificial-intelligence-assisted spatial scoring are mapped to the same evidence requirements. MICAT is intended as a reproducible tool for pharmacological go/no-go decisions rather than a claim that target modulation alone constitutes therapeutic immune conversion.

articles.title: Gut microbiota and treatment response heterogeneity across pharmacological therapies for MASH.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive liver disease with increasing global prevalence. However, substantial inter-individual variability in therapeutic response remains a major challenge for effective disease management. Although the gut microbiota is well recognized as a key contributor to MASH pathogenesis, its role in shaping pharmacological treatment response remains insufficiently understood and underexplored in clinical contexts. In this Review, we summarize evidence suggesting that gut microbiota-associated metabolites, including bile acids, short-chain fatty acids, sphingolipids, and other microbial products, may contribute to variability in therapeutic response across major pharmacological classes for MASH, including FXR agonists, PPAR agonists, FGF19/FGF21 analogues, thyroid hormone receptor-β agonists, and incretin-based therapies. However, for most therapeutic classes, direct clinical evidence linking microbiota features to inter-individual treatment response remains limited, and much of the mechanistic evidence is derived from preclinical studies. We integrate current evidence into a response-oriented conceptual framework linking microbiome composition and metabolic activity to biological processes relevant to drug efficacy. This framework identifies priorities for the prospective validation of microbiome-derived biomarkers and microbiome-informed patient stratification in MASH.

articles.title: Charting the N-acyl lipid landscape and decoding their immune dialogues.
PPARγ signaling pathway: strategies and limitations of natural compounds in the treatment of ulcerative colitis.
articles.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory bowel disease characterized by persistent inflammatory activation, immune dysregulation, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and damage to the mucosal barrier. Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) is a key nuclear receptor involved in maintaining intestinal immunity and mucosal homeostasis. Reduced PPARγ expression or impaired function may weaken its negative regulatory role in pro-inflammatory signaling and disrupt the Th17/Treg balance, macrophage polarization, gut microbiota homeostasis, and barrier integrity, making PPARγ a crucial molecular hub linking multiple pathological processes in UC. Due to their structural diversity and multi-target regulatory properties, natural compounds are attracting increasing attention as potential modulators of PPARγ-related networks. This review systematically summarizes the current preclinical evidence regarding natural compounds that target PPARγ and its associated signaling networks in UC, with particular emphasis on their roles in regulating inflammatory responses, immune cell function, the Th17/Treg balance, the gut microbiota, and mucosal barrier integrity through PPARγ-related pathways (including AMPK, NF-κB, mTOR, SIRT1, MAPK, Nrf2, and STAT). Importantly, the currently available evidence primarily stems from in vitro cellular and in vivo animal studies; therefore, it mainly provides mechanistic and preclinical support rather than evidence of clinical efficacy. Current research is also limited by insufficient evaluation of specific targets, reliance on a limited range of disease models, and inadequate characterization of pharmacokinetic and safety profiles. Future research should prioritize rigorous evaluation of PPARγ-dependent mechanisms, conduct pharmacokinetic and safety assessments, and design rigorous human studies and clinical trials to establish the therapeutic potential of these natural compounds in UC. This review provides a framework for critically evaluating the existing evidence and guiding the development and evaluation of PPARγ-targeting natural compounds for UC.

articles.title: Treatment of vascular dementia based on neuroprotection and neural repair strategies: from pathophysiology to natural products.
articles.abstract: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a heterogeneous cognitive disorder associated with cerebrovascular pathology and persistent vascular dysfunction. Because effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited, natural products have attracted interest as potential interventions for the complex pathology of VaD. This review examines their effects from two complementary perspectives: neuroprotection and neural repair. Experimental studies indicate that natural products can influence several interconnected processes, including redox imbalance, neuroinflammation, cell survival, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, vascular remodeling, neurogenesis, and synaptic plasticity. However, the available evidence varies considerably among isolated compounds, botanical extracts, and herbal formulations. Some isolated compounds have been supported by relatively coherent relationships between molecular targets, tissue responses, and functional outcomes, whereas evidence from clinical studies remains much more limited. We therefore consider the current mechanistic evidence together with the major challenges in pharmacokinetics, quality control, and clinical translation.

articles.title: Acute respiratory distress syndrome subphenotypes: the translational path from pathobiology to precision medicine.
articles.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a highly heterogeneous critical illness syndrome lacking effective targeted therapies, partly due to the diverse patient population. Subphenotype research aims to identify homogeneous patient subgroups sharing common biological, physiological, or clinical characteristics, enabling prognostic and predictive enrichment. This review systematically summarizes current ARDS subphenotype research, from pathobiological mechanisms to multidimensional identification based on etiology, imaging, biomarkers, respiratory mechanics, and transcriptomics. We highlight evidence for differential prognoses and treatment responses across subphenotypes, including variable effects of neuromuscular blockade, corticosteroids, and prone positioning. We further discuss challenges and future directions in translating subphenotype classification into bedside practice. This article provides a theoretical framework and practical guidance for advancing precision medicine in ARDS.

articles.title: Availability of age-stratified evidence for GLP1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors: an analysis of European public assessment reports with a focus on older patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: GLP1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors are widely prescribed and their use is increasingly frequent in older patient populations. We evaluated the extent to which older patients were represented in clinical trials of liraglutide, dulaglutide, semaglutide, tirzepatide, dapagliflozin and empagliflozin. METHODS: To identify relevant trials, we screened the respective European Public Assessment Reports (n = 28) and the European Summaries of Product Characteristics (n = 9) for each of the six approved medicines. Further information was retrieved from the original publications of the identified trials and from the ClinicalTrials.gov database (n = 40). Overall, we analyzed n = 185 sources for 106 trial populations. RESULTS: For 46% of the 106 analyzed trial populations, data for patients ≥65 years were identified. Where age distributions were reported, patients aged 75 years or older were markedly underrepresented in nearly all trials, and subgroup analyses of efficacy and safety by age were rarely published. Especially in cardiovascular outcome trials and trials including patients with chronic kidney disease or chronic heart failure, older patients were better represented and analyses of primary outcomes in different age groups were published more frequently. Safety data on different age groups were mainly identified in the European Public Assessment Reports. Whereas increasing numbers of adverse events with older age were observed in several trials, this increase typically affected all trial arms, independent of the drug treatment. CONCLUSION: Data availability for patients with older age is insufficient from pivotal trials to properly describe efficacy or safety of liraglutide, dulaglutide, semaglutide, tirzepatide, dapagliflozin, or empagliflozin.

articles.title: Subcutaneous drug delivery: from simple release testing to biomimetic systems.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Subcutaneous (SC) administration is increasingly used for biologics and long-acting therapeutics, yet formulation performance and human bioavailability remain difficult to predict. This is because the injection site is a heterogenous environment comprising extracellular matrix, interstitial fluid, tissue-resident cells, and distinct vascular and lymphatic vessels. AREAS COVERED: This review evaluates 17-year SC drug-delivery growth, market trends, and in vitro tools spanning shake-flask, dialysis, USP apparatus 4, and biomimetic acellular platforms including SCISSOR, BioJect, ESCAR, and hydrogel-based membrane-inserts. Cellular and microphysiological systems, including 3D adipose models, SubCuTIS, and lymphatics-on-chip, are assessed alongside in silico approaches. Peer-reviewed studies and industry and regulatory reports are evaluated for physiological relevance, accessibility, validation, and translational utility. EXPERT OPINION: Progress has been substantial, but no current model independently reproduces the mechanisms governing human SC absorption. Cellular components remain underutilized despite extensive foundational work in related fields. Priorities include physiologically characterized matrices, realistic interstitial fluids, quantitative mass-balance endpoints, and multicenter validation against human pharmacokinetic data. A modular, fit-for-purpose qualification strategy offers the most practical route toward predictive and animal-sparing SC drug development.

articles.title: Glycol chitosan thermogels: a versatile platform for advanced drug delivery.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Injectable thermogels are promising localized drug delivery platforms as their temperature-triggered in situ gelation facilitates practical administration. However, conventional systems suffer from high critical gelation concentrations, limited biodegradability, cytotoxicity, or acidic degradation, which can cause local inflammation. Glycol chitosan (GC)-based thermogels have emerged as a promising alternative, combining aqueous solubility at physiological pH, biodegradability, biocompatibility, mucoadhesion, low-concentration gelation, and structural versatility. AREAS COVERED: This review comprehensively examines GC-based thermogels, highlighting how hydrophobic modifications govern their structure-property relationships and thermo-responsive gelation. It evaluates their performance as localized reservoirs for small-molecule drugs, biomacromolecules, and genes across challenging anatomical sites with rapid physiological clearance, including ocular, inner ear, and vaginal sites, while summarizing emerging biofunctional applications in cell delivery, wound healing, and 3D biofabrication. Recent advances in prodrug thermogels, dual crosslinked networks, and biohybrid formulations are also discussed. EXPERT OPINION: To advance GC-based thermogels toward clinical implementation, formulation design must prioritize controlled degradation synchronized with payload release and therapeutic duration. Translation will require standardized polymer characterization, reproducible and scalable manufacturing, sterilization-compatible processing, long-term local safety assessment, and rigorous benchmarking in clinically relevant models. Ultimately, indication-specific formulations with functionality tailored to defined therapeutic needs are more likely to achieve clinical translation than a universal platform approach.

articles.title: Inappropriate prescribing of gastric acid suppressants: A systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: AIM: Inappropriate prescribing of gastric acid suppressants (GASs) may compromise treatment outcomes. This study aimed to examine the prevalence of inappropriate prescribing of GASs in all healthcare settings. METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered systematic literature review used PubMed and Embase databases to identify original English-language studies published between 1 January 2000 and 15 December 2025. Studies reporting the number of inappropriate GASs prescribing among patients receiving GASs were included. EndNote, Rayyan and ASReview were used to select studies. RESULTS: Overall, 141 studies from 44 countries were included. The number of patients in the studies ranged from 36 to 922 436. The pooled prevalence of inappropriate prescribing for all continents was 53% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 49% to 57%), prediction interval 15% to 89%, I2 = 99.9% and τ2 = 0.92. Doi plots of the publication bias analysis showed asymmetry in some models (Luis Furuya-Kanamori index = -4.48), but the Copas-adjusted estimate for the overall dataset was essentially identical to the unadjusted pooled estimate, indicating that although small-study effects may be present, publication bias is unlikely to affect the overall pooled prevalence. Based on our dataset, we selected several moderators to evaluate. From the selected moderators, we found that the study setting was the factor significantly associated with differences in the pooled prevalence (P = 0.02). CONCLUSION: Across published studies, approximately half of prescribed GASs was classified as inappropriate. This result highlights the global need for healthcare providers to effectively prevent and discontinue the inappropriate prescribing of GASs.

articles.title: Exercise alleviates high-salt diet-induced locomotor and cardiac dysfunction via muscle Parkin-dependent and -independent mechanisms in Drosophila.
articles.abstract: Parkin encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in mitophagy and oxidative stress regulation. Its role in high-salt diet (HSD)-induced muscle and cardiac damage, and in exercise-mediated protection, remains unclear. Using the UAS/GAL4 system, we achieved muscle-specific Parkin modulation in adult Drosophila and subjected flies to two-week HSD with or without exercise. In normal w1118 flies, HSD impaired climbing endurance and cardiac function, accompanied by decreased Parkin, Pink1, and Atg8a mRNA expression, reduced PGC-1α expression, lower ATP content and mitochondrial density, disrupted SOD/ROS balance, and decreased Mhc, Dys, and MHC protein levels. Muscle-specific Parkin knockdown exacerbated HSD-induced impairments, whereas Parkin overexpression attenuated them. Notably, exercise rescued HSD-induced deficits in Parkin knockdown flies, with restoration of Parkin-related gene expression, mitochondrial biogenesis and function, redox balance, and muscle structural markers. These findings indicate that muscle Parkin expression modulates susceptibility to HSD-induced skeletal muscle and cardiac dysfunction, and that exercise confers protection through both Parkin-dependent and Parkin-independent mechanisms. It is important to emphasize that the observed changes in Parkin, Pink1, Atg8a, PGC-1α, Mhc, and Dys mRNA expression represent changes in gene expression under specific experimental conditions and should not be interpreted as direct transcriptional regulation by Parkin. Parkin is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that acts primarily at the post-translational level; therefore, the observed transcriptional changes may reflect secondary responses to HSD, exercise, or altered mitochondrial quality control rather than direct transcriptional targets of Parkin.

articles.title: Synergistic anti-glioma activity of temozolomide and simvastatin through inhibition of the EGFR/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Glioma is the most aggressive primary tumor of the central nervous system, and acquired resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) is a leading cause of treatment failure and tumor recurrence. Statins are well-tolerated lipid-lowering agents with emerging anti-tumor potential; however, their effects in combination with TMZ against glioma remain incompletely characterized. In this study, we identified simvastatin (SIM) as the most potent statin against U87 cells and systematically evaluated the anti-glioma activity of TMZ plus SIM in vitro and in vivo. The combination markedly inhibited U87 glioma cell proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis while promoting apoptosis. Compared with either monotherapy, the combined regimen exerted superior anti-tumor effects. Mechanistically, TMZ plus SIM suppressed the epidermal growth factor receptor/protein kinase B/mechanistic target of rapamycin (EGFR/AKT/mTOR) signaling axis, a key pathway involved in glioma growth and survival. Importantly, the combination was well tolerated, with no detectable systemic toxicity or disruption of lipid metabolism. Collectively, these findings indicate that TMZ combined with SIM exerts synergistic anti-glioma activity and may represent a potential drug-repurposing strategy for malignant glioma.

articles.title: Piceatannol alleviates silica-induced pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis by inhibiting the SYK/PKCδ/CARD9-BCL10-MALT1/NF-κB signaling-mediated pyroptosis in macrophages.
articles.abstract: Occupational silica exposure is a critical health hazard, leading to silicosis, a debilitating lung disease characterized by persistent inflammation and progressive fibrosis, in which macrophages play a pivotal pathogenic role. This study aimed to evaluate the protective effects of piceatannol (PIC), a natural stilbenoid, against silica-induced pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis, and to elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms. In vivo, PIC administration significantly alleviated acute pulmonary inflammation in a 7-day silica exposure model and reduced chronic fibrosis in a 28-day model, concomitant with suppressed macrophage infiltration into lung tissue. In vitro, PIC suppressed the secretion of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic cytokines from silica-stimulated macrophages and inhibited the subsequent activation of fibroblasts in the co-culture system. Transcriptomic and mechanistic analyses revealed that PIC blocked the SYK/PKCδ/CARD9-BCL10-MALT1/NF-κB signaling axis and downstream NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis in macrophages. Importantly, the therapeutic effects of PIC were reversed by the PKC agonist phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), confirming the specificity of this pathway. These findings identify PIC as a potential therapeutic agent for silicosis that functions by targeting the SYK/PKCδ/CARD9-BCL10-MALT1/NF-κB axis in macrophages and provide new insights into mitigating the pathogenic processes of silica-induced lung disease.

articles.title: Bakuchiol mitigates neuronal dysfunction in estrogen deficient chronic unpredictable mild stress rats: insights from in vivo and in-silico studies.
articles.abstract: Estrogen deficiency in post-menopausal women leads to the development of neurodegenerative disorders. Phytoestrogens are plant-derived compounds that represent novel and safer alternatives to hormone replacement therapy for the treatment of neurological disorders in postmenopausal complications. Bakuchiol is a phytoestrogen exhibiting selective estrogen like effects. The present study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective and antidepressant potential of bakuchiol in ovariectomised rats subjected to chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) exposure. Adult Female Wistar rats were bilaterally ovariectomised (OVX) and subjected to CUMS over a period of four weeks in order to mimic the development of depression and cognitive deficits in menopause. At the end of the study, basic physiological and neurobehavioral parameters, biochemical estimation, and serum corticosterone levels were evaluated. Levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), Acetylcholinesterase were evaluated and histopathological changes were also studied. In silico Molecular docking studies carried out against proteins TrkB receptor (PDB ID: 4AT5) and Human Acetylcholinesterase (PDB ID: 4EY7). Molecular dynamics studies carried out to study ligand-protein interaction stability. Treatment with bakuchiol and 17-β estradiol (E2) significantly restores the pathological changes towards normal levels. However, the protective effect of bakuchiol was completely abolished when administered in the presence of Fulvestrant in OVX + CUMS groups of rats. The in-silico results further corroborate the observed in vitro results. Bakuchiol showed binding affinities of -6.052 kcal/mol and -5.493 kcal/mol toward BDNF-TrkB and AChE, respectively showing its neurotrophic and antidepressant effects. Molecular dynamics studies also supported these results via showing stable and energetically favoured interactions of Bakuchiol with BDNF-TrkB and acetylcholinesterase. Our current study shows that Bakuchiol at doses of 20 & 40 mg/kg dose dependently possess the potential to alleviate the neurological disorder in estrogen deficient chronic stress conditions.

articles.title: Evodiamine inhibits lung cancer by rectifying abnormal glycolysis via the AMPK signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Evodiamine (EVO) is a principal bioactive compound derived from Evodiae Fructus and is widely used in Asian countries. Accumulating evidence suggests that EVO has potential anticancer activity, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the anti-lung cancer effect of EVO and the corresponding mechanism. Mouse xenograft models and lung cancer cell lines were employed to evaluate the inhibitory effect of EVO. Transcriptomics, metabolomics, and network pharmacology were applied to investigate the underlying mechanism, which was further verified by performing targeted metabolomics, siRNA transfection, specific inhibitor treatment and molecular docking analysis. The results indicated that EVO significantly inhibited tumor growth in xenograft-bearing mice, inhibited the proliferation, invasion, and migration of lung cancer cells, induced cell cycle arrest, and promoted apoptosis. Further analysis revealed that EVO rectified abnormal glycolysis in lung cancer cells via the adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling pathway, as evidenced by reduced lactate production and increased levels of tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates. EVO markedly increased AMPK phosphorylation levels, and AMPK knockdown or treatment with a specific inhibitor significantly attenuated its anticancer effect. Molecular docking results indicated strong interactions between EVO and AMPK. In conclusion, EVO exerts anti-lung cancer effects by rectifying abnormal glycolysis through the regulation of the AMPK signaling pathway.

articles.title: p97 inhibition attenuates cigarette Smoke-Induced lung inflammation and epithelial senescence by Restoring SIRT1 SUMOylation.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is driven by cigarette smoke-induced lung inflammation and accelerated epithelial senescence, yet the upstream regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we investigate the role of the AAA + ATPase p97 in regulating SIRT1 post-translational modification and its contribution to pulmonary pathology. Mouse lung epithelial TC-1 cells were exposed to 5% cigarette smoke extract (CSE); cellular senescence was assessed by SA-β-gal staining, cytokine ELISA, and Western blotting. The regulatory axis was dissected using the p97 inhibitor CB-5083 and the SUMOylation inhibitor 2-D08. In vivo relevance was validated in a murine COPD model combining cigarette smoke (CS) exposure with intranasal LPS challenge. CSE exposure upregulated p97 while downregulating SIRT1 and SUMO1, concomitant with elevated IL-6 and IL-1β secretion. Pharmacological inhibition of p97 with CB-5083 attenuated the senescent phenotype, restored SIRT1 stability and deacetylase activity, and enhanced SIRT1-SUMO1 conjugation. Critically, the SUMOylation inhibitor 2-D08 abrogated these protective effects of CB-5083. In vivo, CB-5083 administration markedly ameliorated CS + LPS-induced alveolar damage, neutrophilic infiltration, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production; these benefits were significantly reversed by co-administration of 2-D08. These findings indicate that p97 promotes cigarette smoke-induced lung inflammation and epithelial senescence by impairing SIRT1 SUMOylation-dependent stability and activity, identifying the p97-SIRT1-SUMO1 axis as a novel pharmacological target for COPD therapy.

articles.title: Benzoquinoplatin, an Apurinic/Apyrimidinic site Adduct-Forming Agent, Disables APE1 repair and overcomes cancer chemoresistance.
articles.abstract: Apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites are abundant but normally short-lived intermediates of base excision repair because they are rapidly processed by AP endonuclease 1 (APE1). Here, we identify benzoquinoplatin (BQP), a benzoquinoline complex with a monofunctional platinum(II) moiety, as an AP-site-directed adduct-former that covalently traps DNA lesions. Following incubation with AP-containing DNA and removal of unbound compound, benzoquinoplatin rendered the lesion refractory to APE1-mediated cleavage, demonstrating that repair was disrupted at the substrate level rather than through direct inhibition of the enzyme. Computational modelling supports a dual mechanism where benzoquinoplatin occupies the AP site and positions Pt for neighbor-base adduct formation. In cancer cells, benzoquinoplatin induced sustained phosphorylated histone H2AX (γH2AX) signalling, cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, and durable suppression of proliferative capacity. Consistent with this mechanism, benzoquinoplatin exhibits markedly enhanced cytotoxic and antiproliferative effects compared with cisplatin in multiple cancer cell lines. Importantly, benzoquinoplatin retains potent activity in cisplatin-resistant cancer cells and effectively suppresses tumor growth in resistant xenograft models in vivo. Furthermore, benzoquinoplatin demonstrates synergistic interactions with poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibition, as cooperative disruption of DNA repair pathways amplifies cytotoxic efficacy. Collectively, these findings identify benzoquinoplatin as a DNA repair-interfering platinum agent that induces persistent DNA damage and overcomes cisplatin resistance. This work highlights a strategy for targeting DNA repair intermediates to enhance the efficacy of platinum-based chemotherapy and provides a framework for the development of next-generation platinum therapeutics.

articles.title: A recombinant CD99-targeted antibody-drug conjugate for Ewing sarcoma therapy.
articles.abstract: Ewing sarcoma (ES) is an aggressive paediatric malignancy characterised by high CD99 expression and limited targeted therapeutic options. In this study, we developed a recombinant anti-CD99 Cancer Institute Antibody (CIAb-anti-CD99) by isotype switching a hybridoma-derived IgM/κ antibody to an IgG2a/κ format to improve manufacturability and therapeutic applicability. Recombinant CIAb-anti-CD99 was expressed in CHO-K1 cells and retained specific recognition of CD99, as demonstrated by immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Functionally, CIAb-anti-CD99 increased the Annexin V/PI-positive cell population and inhibited proliferation and clonogenic growth of CD99-positive ES cells in vitro. To evaluate the potential of CIAb-anti-CD99 for targeted drug delivery, CIAb-anti-CD99 was conjugated to doxorubicin to generate a CD99-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (CIAb-Dox). In vivo biodistribution studies demonstrated tumour localisation and prolonged retention of CIAb-anti-CD99 in A673 xenograft tumours. Therapeutic evaluation in an A673 cell line-derived xenograft (CDX) model showed that CIAb-Dox significantly suppressed tumour growth compared with vehicle and antibody monotherapy. Histopathological analysis demonstrated lower viable tumour content and greater tumour necrosis in CIAb-Dox-treated tumours. Quantitative immunohistochemical analysis further showed a significant reduction in the Ki67-positive proliferative index and increased cleaved PARP staining, consistent with apoptosis-associated cellular changes. CIAb-Dox demonstrated enhanced antitumour activity while maintaining a favourable tolerability profile. Collectively, these findings provide preclinical evidence supporting further investigation of CD99-directed antibody-drug conjugates. CIAb-anti-CD99 represents a functionally active CD99-targeting antibody, while CIAb-Dox warrants further evaluation in additional Ewing sarcoma models, together with mechanistic, pharmacokinetic, and comprehensive analytical studies.

articles.title: Unveiling the mechanisms of nephrotoxicity caused by the interplay of losartan and febuxostat.
articles.abstract: Hypertension and hyperuricemia are commonly comorbid conditions. Losartan and febuxostat are frequently used therapeutic agents for hypertension and hyperuricemia respectively. However, the long-term impacts of their combined administration, particularly on kidneys, are still largely unknown. Through establishing a rat model of hypertension with hyperuricemia, this study investigated renal outcomes under different therapeutic regimens. We implemented a multimodal omics strategy including transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis, followed by multidimensional validation, to further explore the mechanisms underlying the specific nephrotoxicity induced by the combination of losartan and febuxostat. Our findings demonstrated that although the combined use of losartan and febuxostat effectively reduced serum uric acid and blood pressure levels, it paradoxically induced significant renal injury. The nephrotoxicity predominantly originated from activation of the Atf4-Ddit3/Chac1 pathway in renal distal convoluted tubules following the coadministration of losartan and febuxostat, which sequentially induced stress response and glutathione hydrolysis, followed by oxidative stress damage, and ultimately apoptosis. This study provides the first evidence indicating the potential renal risks of the combined treatment regimen of losartan and febuxostat in patients with hypertension and hyperuricemia.

articles.title: Placental and lactational transfer of lead across the perinatal continuum: a proof-of-concept extended PBPK model calibrated with longitudinal data from two independent human birth cohorts.
articles.abstract: Lead (Pb) exposure during the perinatal period poses significant neurodevelopmental risks to the fetus and infant, yet no physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model has characterized the full maternal-placental-lactational Pb continuum for East Asian populations. This study develops and validates an extended perinatal continuum PBPK model using longitudinal biomonitoring data from two independent Korean birth cohorts: Ko-CHENS (n = 3625 mother-infant triads with serial blood Pb at early pregnancy [T1], late pregnancy [T2], and cord blood) and NOEMOC (n = 242 with urinary and breast milk Pb). Three pre-PBPK statistical analyses informed model parameterization. Linear mixed-effects modeling identified an 8.1% T1-to-T2 blood lead decline consistent with hemodilution, with serum calcium, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and smoking as key modifiers; and feto-maternal ratio regression (GM = 0.760) showed that the feto-maternal ratio declines with increasing maternal blood Pb (β = -0.503), a pattern that is incompatible with purely first-order passive diffusion and indicates a saturable component of placental Pb handling. Urinary Pb increased from early to late pregnancy under every dilution-correction metric (paired n = 152), indicating a genuine rise in renal Pb excretion consistent with the gestational increase in glomerular filtration. Bayesian MCMC calibration yielded population-specific estimates of a later onset (start time of additional pregnancy-related bone remodeling, STBR = 24.45 weeks fetal age, 95% CrI 22.66-26.86) and a smaller magnitude (coefficient of additional bone remodeling, CABR = 0.364 week-1, 95% CrI 0.223-1.022) than the European-derived reference parameterization, together with a placental permeability coefficient KD_pl = 0.044 L·day-1·dm-2 (95% CrI 0.018-0.060). The model reproduced the observed feto-maternal ratio without any post hoc rescaling (predicted GM 0.785 vs observed 0.756) and was unbiased for both maternal late-pregnancy blood Pb (MFE 1.007) and cord blood Pb (MFE 1.046). The mixed-effects PBPK best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP) framework achieved W₂fold = 100% for cord blood prediction, with hold-out external validation (n = 716; deterministic W₂fold 84.2% for maternal and 75.6% for cord blood Pb) confirming generalizability. Breast milk Pb GM (0.107 μg/L) remained below levels of immediate toxicological concern, with the lactational pathway evaluated against infant blood Pb at six months of age (n = 1874). This model provides a mechanistic, individual-level framework for perinatal Pb exposure characterization. Although calibrated on Korean data, the workflow is presented as a transferable proof-of-concept that can be re-applied to any birth cohort with serial maternal, cord and milk biomonitoring; the complete model code is publicly available.

articles.title: Effect of ursodeoxycholic acid on the pharmacokinetics of enalapril and its active metabolite enalaprilat in mice: Implications for transporter-mediated drug-drug interaction.
articles.abstract: Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) has been reported to alter the expression of hepatic transporters, such as organic anion-transporting polypeptides (OATPs), and multidrug resistance-associated proteins (MRPs). This study investigated the pharmacokinetic interactions between UDCA and enalapril-a substrate of hepatic Oatp1a1 and Mrp2-and its active metabolite enalaprilat, a substrate of Mrp4 and organic anion transporter 3 (Oat3), in mice fed a 1% UDCA-diet for seven days. In UDCA-diet mice, hepatic Oatp1a1 and Oatp1b2 mRNA expression levels were significantly reduced, whereas Mrp4 expression was upregulated. Following an intravenous bolus of enalapril (2 mg/kg), UDCA-diet mice exhibited increased systemic exposure (AUC0-∞) and peak plasma concentration (Cmax) of enalapril, whereas the hepatic distribution and volume of distribution at steady state (Vss) declined. Consequently, the ratio of the area under the plasma concentration-time curve for enalaprilat to that for enalapril (AUCm/AUCp) decreased. Although the total area under the plasma concentration-time curve from time zero to infinity (AUC0-∞) for enalaprilat remained unchanged, Cmax increased. Furthermore, the renal clearance of enalaprilat decreased, potentially due to UDCA-mediated inhibition of renal Oat3. These findings demonstrate that high UDCA exposure alters the disposition of enalapril and enalaprilat by modulating hepatic and renal transporters, supporting the potential for transporter-associated drug interactions under elevated UDCA exposure.

articles.title: Chrysene aggravates allergic airway inflammation in association with TRPA1/NF-κB signaling and epithelial-immune dysregulation.
articles.abstract: Chrysene, a representative polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), is a ubiquitous environmental pollutant associated with adverse respiratory health effects. However, the mechanisms by which chrysene contributes to allergic airway inflammation remain incompletely understood. The present study investigated the involvement of TRPA1/NF-κB signaling in chrysene-associated epithelial injury and epithelial-immune dysregulation. Human bronchial epithelial cells and an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced murine model of allergic airway inflammation were used. Chrysene exposure inhibited epithelial cell proliferation, increased reactive oxygen species generation, enhanced TRPA1/NF-κB signaling, and reduced the expression of epithelial junction-associated proteins, including E-cadherin, ZO-1, and occludin. Pharmacological inhibition or lentiviral-mediated knockdown of TRPA1 attenuated NF-κB signaling and partially restored junction-associated protein expression. In vivo, chrysene aggravated OVA-induced airway hyperresponsiveness, eosinophilic inflammation, and mucus hypersecretion. These changes were accompanied by increased serum IL-25, IL-33, and TSLP levels, enhanced pulmonary ILC2 responses, and elevated serum IL-5 and IL-13 levels. Inhibition of TRPA1 or NF-κB attenuated several of these responses. Overall, these findings implicate TRPA1/NF-κB signaling in chrysene-associated epithelial injury and type 2 allergic airway inflammation.

articles.title: Overcoming delivered volume limitations of double-jet impinging atomizers; development of alternative soft mist generation concepts.
articles.abstract: Atomization in the Respimat® relies on impinging microjets. Reorienting the twin jets toward a maximized included angle improves energy transfer, enabling aerosolization at reduced pressure and thereby expanding the design space for higher delivered volumes per actuation. However, this potential optimization is constrained by a trade-off between droplet breakup efficiency and backward-directed spray, causing elevated losses at the nozzle outlet. This trade-off was characterized and motivated the evaluation of alternative soft mist generation concepts. Jet-baffle prototypes were developed in which a single liquid jet impacts perpendicularly (corresponding to 180° between two jets) onto a solid surface. An initial approach with an integrated baffle inside the Uniblock provided high aerosol output but required high internal velocity to generate ∼ 5µm droplets, potentially due to droplet coalescence within the confined near-nozzle region. Repositioning the baffle outside the nozzle provided additional space for atomization, enabled small aerosol droplets and allowed for increased delivered volumes per actuation. Radial droplet dispersion following baffle impact emerged as key driver of mouthpiece deposition and aerosol delivery efficiency. The single-jet concept was translated into functional prototypes. Compared with the standard Respimat device, these prototypes operated at similar jet velocity but lower operating pressure and reduced shear rates within the nozzle microchannel, suggesting gentler aerosolization. Testing with selected biologic formulations indicated better preservation of biologic integrity than with the standard Respimat device and a vibrating mesh nebulizer. Overall, the single-jet design represents a promising approach to extend the Respimat inhaler family toward lower-potency, less soluble, and shear-sensitive therapeutics.

articles.title: Hybrid Alginate/Eudragit L100 microgels fabricated by microfluidics for intestinal delivery of lipophilic drugs.
articles.abstract: Poor aqueous solubility remains a major barrier to bringing new drug molecules to the market. Approximately 40% of approved drugs and 90% of candidates suffer from inadequate dissolution, resulting in aggregation, uncontrolled release, and reduced bioavailability. In this study, we developed a dual-stage Tesla-assisted flow-focusing (DiTAFF) microfluidic platform for the on-chip fabrication of Alginate (Alg)/Eudragit® L100 (EL100) hybrid microgels (HybMGs) containing melatonin (Mel). A water-miscible organic EL100/Mel phase enabled the incorporation of the hydrophobic payload into the hydrophilic Alg matrix during droplet formation, while the chip allowed adjustment of the polymer ratio and acid-triggered pregelation before external Ca2⁺ curing. Microgel (MG) diameter and organic-phase concentration were controlled through on-chip flow parameters, and the 17:3 inlet flow-rate ratio was selected as the process-optimized condition using a β parameter that balances the relative EL100/Mel precursor feed contribution against droplet-size variability. LE increased from 0.35 ± 0.04% for Alg MGs to 0.91 ± 0.05% for IPA-derived HybMGs and 0.78 ± 0.06% for MeOH-derived HybMGs, corresponding to 2.60-fold and 2.23-fold increases, respectively. At pH 2.0, drug retention was ∼ 58% (Alg), ∼71% (IPA), and ∼ 86% (MeOH); at pH 7.4, MeOH-derived MGs released Mel faster than IPA-derived MGs. Mel-loaded HybMGs maintained ∼ 100% L929 cell viability. The resulting platform provides an optimized, tunable, reproducible, and Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)-compatible microfluidic process for fabricating polysaccharide-enteric polymer HybMGs as tunable carriers for the intestinal delivery of lipophilic drugs.

articles.title: Integrating binder and powder rheology to understand granulation behavior in twin-screw melt granulation.
articles.abstract: Twin-screw melt granulation (TSMG) is governed by the interplay between binder softening and powder flow as the formulation passes through the heated extruder. Binder softening modifies particle-particle and powder-wall friction, influencing granulation and product quality. Silica was incorporated at different concentrations to investigate its influence on binder rheology, powder rheology, and granulation performance under process-relevant temperatures. Powder blends containing 95:5 w/w acetaminophen/Klucel Fusion™ X hydroxypropyl cellulose (binder) and 0.05-1% w/w silica were prepared. Powder shear-cell measurements at 80 and 100 °C determined the effective angle of internal friction, flow function coefficient, wall friction angle, and conditional bulk density, while oscillatory rheology characterized the binder's viscoelasticity in the presence of 0-1% w/w silica. These rheological properties were correlated with system parameters (minimum feed rate-to-screw speed ratio (Q/N) required for successful granulation and specific mechanical energy (SME)) and product attributes (granule size and tabletability). Increasing silica concentration reduced binder's tan(δ), indicating lower mobility of molecular units in the binder, and altered powder rheology in a concentration-dependent manner. Formulations containing up to 0.2% silica exhibited greater interparticle cohesion, allowing successful granulation at lower Q/N ratios with less SME while maintaining satisfactory tabletability. Increasing silica to 0.5 and 1% reduced interparticle cohesion, increased wall friction and SME requirements, and required a higher Q/N ratio for successful granulation. Overall, binder rheology and powder rheology evolved concurrently during TSMG and collectively governed granulation performance. Characterizing these complementary rheological properties under process-relevant conditions provides a practical, material-efficient framework for interpreting granulation behavior and developing robust TSMG formulations.

articles.title: Analysis of the pH-dependent phase behavior of amorphous solid dispersions using in situ stimulated Raman scattering microscopy.
articles.abstract: In this study, in situ stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy was employed as a novel analytical method to investigate the pH-dependent phase behavior of amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) during hydration. Ibuprofen-poly(1-vinylpyrrolidone-co-vinyl acetate) (IBU-PVPVA) ASDS were used as model systems. The ASDs underwent multiple structural changes including polymer swelling, gel-layer formation and phase separation. To monitor these processes, binary IBU-PVPVA ASDs with six drug loadings were studied under four pH conditions using in situ hyperspectral stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy with spectral focusing, further augmented with correlative confocal reflection imaging. Spectral imaging data analysis was performed with classical least squares, preceded by multivariate curve resolution-alternating least squares estimation. Supportive solid-state analysis was performed using modulated temperature differential scanning calorimetry, polarized light microscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and spontaneous Raman spectroscopy combined with principal component analysis. The results show that in situ SRS microscopy enables detailed real-time visualization of pH-dependent structural evolution in ASDs during hydration. The phase behavior was found to be affected by the environmental pH and buffering conditions, expected to ultimately determine drug release performance.

articles.title: Chongcao Qingfei Capsule alleviates house dust mite-induced allergic airway inflammation by regulating metabolic homeostasis via modulation of the PDE7A-cAMP-AMPK-mTOR axis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Chongcao Qingfei Capsule (CCQF) is a Tibetan medicinal formulation used in China for respiratory disorders presenting with cough, excessive sputum, chest tightness, and wheezing. According to its documented traditional therapeutic use, the complete formulation is used to moisten and tonify the lung, clear lung heat and resolve phlegm, and relieve cough and wheezing, particularly in respiratory conditions characterized by qi and yin deficiency with phlegm-heat obstructing the lung. These traditional indications, especially cough, phlegm accumulation, chest tightness, and wheezing, are closely related to the airway manifestations investigated in the present study. However, the pharmacological basis for the effects of CCQF on allergic airway inflammation remains poorly understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the protective effects of CCQF against house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway inflammation and to elucidate its underlying molecular mechanism, thereby providing experimental evidence for its documented traditional use in respiratory disorders characterized by cough, phlegm, chest tightness, and wheezing. MATERIALS AND METHODS: UPLC-Q-Orbitrap-HRMS was used to characterize the chemical constituents of CCQF and identify its serum- and lung-distributed prototype components. An HDM-induced allergic asthma mouse model was established to evaluate the effects of CCQF on asthma. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses were performed to identify CCQF-regulated proteins, metabolites, and pathways. The potential mechanism was further validated in vitro. RESULTS: CCQF markedly alleviated HDM-induced allergic asthma by improving airway hyperresponsiveness and lung inflammation, reducing mucus hypersecretion, eosinophil accumulation, and Th2-type responses. Chemical profiling identified 55 constituents in CCQF, with six and five prototype components detected in serum and lung tissue, respectively, predominantly comprising Stemonaceae alkaloids in the lung. Proteomic and metabolomic analyses showed that CCQF treatment was associated with changes in immune regulation, oxidative stress, and energy metabolism, with AMPK signaling significantly enriched.. PDE7A was identified as a candidate CCQF-responsive protein. CCQF treatment was accompanied by higher cAMP levels, increased AMPK phosphorylation, and partial normalization of metabolic homeostasis. CCQF also improved antioxidant capacity and was associated with reduced HDM-induced mTOR phosphorylation. In HDM-stimulated BEAS-2B cells, CCQF and the PDE7 inhibitor BRL-50481 produced comparable changes, consistent with a possible contribution of PDE7A-cAMP-AMPK-mTOR signaling to the protective effects of CCQF. However, direct target engagement and pathway causality were not established. CONCLUSION: CCQF alleviates HDM-induced allergic asthma by suppressing Th2-type airway inflammation, reducing eosinophilic infiltration and mucus hypersecretion, and restoring pulmonary metabolic and redox homeostasis. These protective effects were accompanied by lower PDE7A abundance, higher cAMP availability, increased AMPK phosphorylation, and reduced mTOR phosphorylation. Because direct PDE7A inhibition and pathway epistasis were not demonstrated, these findings should be interpreted as evidence consistent with, but not proving, a PDE7A-cAMP-AMPK-mTOR contribution. Whether AMPK activation is required for the mTOR effect was not tested. These findings provide candidate mechanistic insight and identify the PDE7A-cAMP-AMPK-mTOR axis as a candidate pathway for further target validation in allergic airway inflammation.

articles.title: Gramine Alleviates Ulcerative Colitis by Targeting COX-2 and Inhibiting Ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Arundo donax Linn is a well-known herbal remedy in traditional healing systems that is commonly indicated for fever, toothache, and dysuria, as documented in the Chinese medicinal literature. Gramine (GRA) is an alkaloid derived from the rhizome of Arundo donax, and studies have confirmed its antiviral, antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer properties. However, its specific pharmacological mechanism in the context of ulcerative colitis (UC) has yet to be systematically elucidated. AIM OF THIS STUDY: The objective of this study was to elucidate the protective role and mechanisms of GRA in UC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Network pharmacology and bioinformatics analyses were performed to identify potential targets associated with UC, ferroptosis, and GRA. The direct binding of GRA to COX-2 was confirmed using surface plasmon resonance (SPR), molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. An in vivo model of UC was established in mice via the administration of 3% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS). In this UC model system, we evaluated the effects of GRA and celecoxib (CEL) alone and in combination. Histopathological changes, intestinal epithelial barrier function, and the levels of ferroptosis-related markers were assessed. Additionally, the combined effects of GRA and CEL on ferroptosis and intestinal barrier integrity were further evaluated in a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated NCM460 cell model of colitis. RESULTS: The network pharmacology analysis identified COX-2 as a core target connecting ferroptosis, UC, and GRA. Direct binding between GRA and COX-2 was subsequently confirmed using molecular docking, MD simulations, and SPR.
