In vivo, GRA treatment significantly reduced the disease activity index (DAI), histological damage, and cell death in mice with colitis. Further investigation revealed the induction of ferroptosis in mice with colitis, as evidenced by iron overload, glutathione (GSH) depletion, increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and upregulated of COX-2 expression. Treatment with GRA, CEL, or their combination significantly ameliorated these ferroptosis-related alterations. Transmission electron microscopy further revealed that GRA counteracted intestinal barrier disruption. Consistently, in vitro experiments demonstrated that all three treatments: GRA, CEL, and GRA + CEL, effectively inhibited ferroptosis and preserved intestinal barrier integrity, thereby mitigating UC pathology. Notably, the results of both in vitro and in vivo experiments indicated that the combination therapy of GRA and CEL (GRA + CEL) exhibited superior efficacy compared with either GRA or CEL treatment alone. CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrated that GRA alleviates UC by protecting the intestinal barrier; notably, GRA + CEL treatment exerted greater therapeutic effects than GRA or CEL alone. The potential underlying mechanism may involve the mitigation of ferroptosis by GRA through the inhibition of COX-2.

articles.title: Inhibition of Hemoglobin S Polymerization and Antiplasmodial Activity of Medicinal Plants Traditionally Used to Manage Sickle Cell Disease in Tanzania.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: While current therapeutic interventions for Sickle Cell Disease (SCD), such as hydroxyurea, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and gene therapy, offer clinical benefits, they remain inaccessible to most patients in developing countries due to side effects, unavailability of donors, and high costs; hence, traditional medicines offer an important alternative. The selected plants have been traditionally used for managing SCD and/or its symptoms in Tanzania; however, there were limited scientific reports supporting their use. Therefore, this study evaluated selected plants traditionally used to manage SCD in Tanzania to explore affordable alternative therapies. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to screen medicinal plants for their in vitro sickle hemoglobin (HbS) polymerization inhibitory and antiplasmodial activities that are traditionally used to manage SCD in Tanzania. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 14 medicinal plants, comprising 22 plant parts (leaves, stems, and roots), were extracted with water (decoction) and 80% methanol. Each crude extract (5 mg/mL) was evaluated for its in vitro hemoglobin S polymerization, hemolytic activity, antiplasmodial activity, and cytotoxicity. RESULTS: This study identified several medicinal plants with in vitro activity in HbS polymerization inhibition and/or antiplasmodial activity. Lonchocarpus eriocalyx leaves exhibited HbS polymerization inhibition (42%) with no hemolytic or cytotoxic effect, while the root barks of Combretum zeyheri and Terminalia mollis exhibited potent antiplasmodial activity; IC50 values were 2.6 and 13.2 μg/mL, and 1.3 and 8.0 μg/mL, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings provide preliminary support for the traditional use of some medicinal plants such as Lonchocarpus eriocalyx and Combretum zeyheri in managing SCD and malaria. Further studies should include chemical profiling of these extracts, isolation of promising constituents, and biological evaluation.

articles.title: Combining brain-penetrating and anticancer peptides into bivalent-branched peptides conserves brain targeting and improves activity in vitro.
articles.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a particularly challenging subtype of breast cancer (BC) due to the absence of common therapeutically targetable receptors, its tendency toward chemoresistance, and its high rates of recurrence and metastasis, particularly to the brain. The development of brain metastases (BM) poses an additional hurdle, largely due to the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Recently, we reported the therapeutic potential of a dual-acting peptide, PepH3-vCPP2319, that combines a BBB peptide shuttle (BBBpS - PepH3) and an anticancer peptide (ACP - vCPP2319) to eliminate TNBC-BM. In vitro, PepH3-vCPP2319 showed high translocation capacity in our transwell system (BBB cross > 40%), high anticancer activity (IC50 ∼ 5.0 µM), and low toxicity (HC50 > 25.0 µM). To further enhance its potency, we designed two bivalent-branched peptides that conjugate two PepH3 sequences and one vCPP2319 sequence, or vice versa. Our results indicated that, compared with PepH3-vCPP2319, both peptides translocated (∼ 40%) across a cellular BBB model and exhibited stronger anticancer activity (IC50 ∼ 2.0 µM) while maintaining moderate toxicity (HC50 > 15.0 µM). Compared with vCPP2319 and PepH3-vCPP2319, both bivalent-branched peptides are internalized quicker in cancer cells without membrane disruption, suggesting an intracellular mechanism of action. In conclusion, our study demonstrates the merit of branched peptide design in keeping the brain delivery and improving the efficacy of ACPs, although with slightly high toxicity, for the treatment of TNBC-BM.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics and target attainment of aztreonam/avibactam in plasma and tissue: A human microdialysis study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study investigated the pharmacokinetics (PK) and target attainment of the novel β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combination aztreonam/avibactam in tissue and plasma. METHODS: Ten healthy volunteers received a single intravenous 3-hour infusion of aztreonam/avibactam 2000/670 mg. Unbound concentrations in plasma (ultrafiltration) and in subcutaneous and intramuscular interstitial fluid (microdialysis, calibrated by retrodialysis) were quantified over 12 h by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. We performed a non-compartmental analysis and assessed the number of participants attaining the joint PK/pharmacodynamic (PD) target of aztreonam 60% fT>MIC and avibactam 50% fT>CT of 2.5 mg/L during the first 6-hour dosing interval. RESULTS: The geometric mean (geometric coefficient of variation) fAUC0-12 of aztreonam was 208.9 (17.3%), 100.5 (39.4%), and 115.3 (36.2%) h·mg/L in plasma, subcutis, and muscle, respectively, and that of avibactam was 63.2 (22.1%), 37.3 (37.6%), and 40.2 (36.7%) h·mg/L. Geometric mean tissue-to-plasma fAUC0-12 ratios were 0.48-0.64. At an aztreonam minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 8 mg/L, the joint target was attained in 10/10 participants in plasma and in 9/10 participants in subcutis and muscle (95% confidence interval 55-100%). CONCLUSION: In healthy volunteers, unbound subcutaneous and muscle exposure of aztreonam/avibactam was approximately half to two-thirds of unbound plasma exposure. Under the conditions studied, most participants attained the joint target up to an MIC of 8 mg/L in all compartments. Studies in patients with skin and soft tissue infections are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: ZeXieYin formula attenuates trimethylamine N-oxide- induced atherosclerosis and cognitive impairment by regulating microglial-neuronal signaling and autophagy.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: ZeXieYin Formula (ZXYF), a classic traditional Chinese medicine decoction first documented in the Huangdi Neijing (an ancient Chinese medical text), traditionally used to treat patterns of internal accumulation of phlegm turbidity and deficiency of healthy qi-a pathogenesis closely associated with atherosclerosis and cognitive impairment, and which is composed of three medicinal herbs-Alisma plantago-aquatica L. (Zexie, Water Plantain Rhizome, dried tuber), Atractylodis macrocephala Koidz. (Baizhu, Largehead Atractylodes Rhizome, dried rhizome), and Pyrola calliantha Andres. (Luxiancao, Chinese Pyrola Herb, whole herb)-in a 2:2:1 ratio. For the preparation of ZXYF decoction, Zexie (200 g), Baizhu (200 g), and Luxiancao (100 g) were accurately weighed. ZXYF has been observed in our previous studies to reduce trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) levels, exert anti-inflammatory and lipid-lowering effects and alleviate atherosclerosis (AS) while improving cognitive function. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate whether ZXYF ameliorates TMAO-induced AS with concurrent cognitive impairment (AS-CI) by modulating microglia-mediated paracrine signaling and subsequent neuroinflammation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: To create an AS-CI model in vivo, Apolipoprotein E-deficient mice(ApoE-/- mice) were given a high-fat diet (containing the TMAO precursor choline) for 8 weeks. ZXYF (6.5, 13 g/kg) was administered via gavage. Aortic plaques were evaluated by Oil Red O staining, cognitive function was detected by behavioral tests (Y-maze, Morris water maze, and novel object recognition), and TMAO levels in brain tissue and serum were examined by Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-ESI-MS/MS). Immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were used to evaluate microglial activation, C-C chemokine receptor type 5 (CCR5) expression, microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3) expression, toxic proteins deposition, and autophagic ultrastructure in the hippocampus. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Western blot were performed to detect the protein expression of chemokines, factors that promote inflammation, and related signaling pathways. In vitro, a paracrine model of BV2 microglia and HT22 neurons was established, and autophagic flux was detected by transfection with green fluorescent protein-red fluorescent protein-LC3 (GFP-RFP-LC3) lentivirus. CCR5 antagonist maraviroc, mTOR inhibitor rapamycin, and ZXYF-containing serum were used for intervention to verify the signaling pathway mechanism. RESULTS: ZXYF treatment significantly reduced aortic plaque area, enhanced working, spatial, and recognition memory (p < 0.05), and concurrently lowered TMAO levels in both brain tissue and serum. ZXYF prevented hippocampus microglial activation and the MAPK/NF-κB inflammatory cascade, and downregulated the release of proinflammatory factors. Mechanistic studies showed that ZXYF markedly reduced the expression of chemokines C-C motif chemokine ligand 3 (CCL3), C-C motif chemokine ligand 4 (CCL4) and C-C motif chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5) in the brain, inhibited the expression of their receptor CCR5 and downstream mTOR phosphorylation, thereby restoring neuronal autophagy (increasing the number of autophagosomes, upregulating LC3-II and Beclin1, and downregulating sequestosome 1 (p62)) and reducing the deposition of amyloid-beta (Aβ) and phosphorylated Tau (p-Tau) proteins. In vitro experiments supported that the conditioned medium of activated microglia induced autophagy inhibition and neuroinflammation through the CCL3/4/5-CCR5-mTOR axis, while maraviroc, rapamycin and ZXYF-containing serum could block this effect and restore autophagic flux. CONCLUSION: ZXYF ameliorates AS-CI by reducing TMAO levels, inhibiting microglial activation and the release of CCL3/4/5, thereby blocking the neuronal CCR5-mTOR signaling axis, restoring autophagic function and alleviating neuroinflammation.

articles.title: Aspirin for primary prevention of cardiovascular mortality: smoking exposure as a potential effect modifier-a cotinine‑based observational analysis.
articles.abstract: Serum cotinine, an objective biomarker of tobacco smoke exposure, may modify the association between regular aspirin use and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) mortality in primary prevention, but this hypothesis has not been adequately tested. We analyzed nationally representative data from NHANES 2011-2018, including 6732 adults aged ≥ 40 years without prior cardiovascular events. Regular aspirin use was defined as ≥ 15 days/month, serum cotinine was measured by mass spectrometry, and the primary outcome was ASCVD mortality. Weighted Cox models assessed associations with interaction terms for aspirin use × smoking status and aspirin use × log‑cotinine. Aspirin use was associated with improved survival in current smokers (fully adjusted HR = 0.15, 95% CI 0.03-0.76), but with worse survival in never smokers (HR = 1.86, 95% CI 1.12-3.10), and a null association in former smokers (HR = 1.65, 95% CI 0.75-3.65). A graded risk attenuation was observed across increasing cotinine tertiles (p for linear interaction = 0.013). Significant interactions were found for both smoking status (p < 0.05) and continuous log‑cotinine (p = 0.009), and sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness. In conclusion, smoking exposure objectively quantified by serum cotinine significantly modifies the observed aspirin-ASCVD mortality association in this observational analysis; biomarker‑informed stratification may offer a framework for hypothesis generation, but prospective validation in randomized trials is essential before any clinical application can be considered.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in drug research: A nested-cohort bibliometric analysis of mechanistic interpretation and model interpretability.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) supports prediction and explanation in drug research. We examined the representation and development of mechanistic interpretation and model interpretability within this literature. Publications from 2000 to 2025 were analysed using Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC), with PubMed providing a complementary perspective. Cohort A comprised eligible AI drug research; B was its subset addressing substantive drug-mechanism analysis and/or drug-related model interpretation. Comparisons contrasted B with A-only using temporal models, lexical analyses, network permutations, matched institutional analyses, and false-discovery-rate correction. WoSCC included 22,542 A publications, including 1324 in B; PubMed included 17,743 and 1048, respectively. From 2020 to 2025, B/A increased from 3.67% to 10.30% in WoSCC and from 3.17% to 10.64% in PubMed. Full-period trends were nonlinear (both P < 0.001). Explanation-related terminology also increased within A-only. Excluding query-linked terms, crude term-association estimates correlated across databases (Spearman ρ = 0.900; approximate 95% CI, 0.883-0.914); 320 WoSCC and 245 PubMed terms remained significant after publication-year and document-type adjustment and multiplicity correction. WoSCC direct-citation and bibliographic-coupling networks showed modest positive cohort assortativity (0.0746 and 0.0865; both q = 0.0005). In WoSCC, B showed greater institutional concentration than matched A-only samples (q < 0.001), without significant interinstitutional collaboration differences. Principal temporal and network directions persisted in screening sensitivity analyses. Mechanistic interpretation and model interpretability represent a growing emphasis within AI drug research, characterised by cross-database lexical concordance and, in WoSCC, modest network differentiation and greater institutional concentration.

articles.title: Quinalphos-induced chromosomal instability, DNA damage, and Bax/Bcl-2 dysregulation in mouse bone marrow: protective effects of piperine.
articles.abstract: Quinalphos (QNP), an organophosphate insecticide, is known to induce genotoxic and cytotoxic effects in non-target organisms. This study evaluated the impact of subacute QNP exposure on chromosomal stability, DNA integrity, and apoptosis-related gene expression in bone marrow cells of male Swiss albino mice, and assessed the genoprotective potential of piperine (PIP), a bioactive compound from Piper nigrum. Mice were allocated into six groups: control (2% gum acacia), QNP I (0.375 mg/kg b.w.), QNP II (0.75 mg/kg b.w.), PIP alone (10 mg/kg b.w.), QNP I + PIP, and QNP II + PIP. All treatments were administered orally for 28 days. Genotoxicity was evaluated using micronucleus, chromosomal aberration, and alkaline comet assays. The expression of Bax and Bcl-2 was assessed by quantitative real-time PCR. QNP exposure produced a dose-dependent increase in micronucleated erythrocytes, chromosomal aberrations, and DNA damage, as indicated by increases in comet assay parameters. QNP upregulated pro-apoptotic Bax and downregulated anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 mRNA expression, consistent with activation of apoptosis-related signalling. Co-administration of PIP reduced several QNP-induced genotoxic alterations, although the magnitude of attenuation varied among endpoints, and did not fully restore Bax/Bcl-2 expression balance. Overall, PIP reduced QNP-induced genotoxic and apoptosis-related changes, although its protective effects were endpoint-specific. These findings suggest that PIP may have potential as a natural candidate for mitigating QNP-associated genetic damage. Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

articles.title: PDK4-associated metabolic alterations and surfactant dysfunction during hyperoxia in dexamethasone-conditioned and vehicle-conditioned NCI-H441 cultures: implications for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.
articles.abstract: Hyperoxic exposure may aggravate epithelial injury and surfactant dysfunction after oxygen supplementation. This study examined PDK4-associated metabolic regulation and surfactant abnormalities during acute hyperoxia in adenocarcinoma-derived NCI-H441 cultures. Methods: Dexamethasone-supported mature-like and vehicle-treated maturation-deficient-like cultures were established using a 10-day air-liquid interface protocol and exposed to normoxia or 80% oxygen for 24 h. Surfactant lipid abundance, apical SP-B output, lamellar-body-associated puncta, surface activity, and epithelial barrier function were evaluated. Seahorse measurements were obtained from a separate 72-h submerged conditioning model. Dichloroacetate and two independent PDK4-targeting siRNAs were used to investigate PDK-associated regulation. Vehicle-treated ALI cultures exhibited lower differentiation-associated marker expression, DPPC output, and epithelial resistance. Hyperoxia was accompanied by epithelial injury, metabolic abnormalities, reduced surfactant lipid abundance and SP-B output, and impaired barrier function. Recovered secretions showed poorer surface activity despite testing at equal total phospholipid concentration. Parallel submerged cultures exhibited reduced respiration and increased glycolytic activity. Increased PDK4 transcript abundance and PDH phosphorylation accompanied these changes. Dichloroacetate treatment and independent PDK4 silencing produced partial improvement in metabolic and surfactant endpoints. The findings supported a contribution of PDK4-associated regulation to hyperoxia-related epithelial and surfactant abnormalities in the tested culture models. They addressed secondary oxygen-induced injury rather than the developmental origin of neonatal RDS. Dexamethasone confounding, separate culture platforms, and the absence of direct carbon-flux measurements limited mechanistic interpretation.

articles.title: Repurposing proton pump inhibitors to restore ceftriaxone activity against multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae: phenotypic, molecular, and in silico evidence.
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae has emerged as one of the most clinically significant multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, with multidrug efflux systems playing a pivotal role in antibiotic resistance and therapeutic failure. This study investigated the contribution of the efflux-associated genes kpnE, kmrA, and kdeA to ceftriaxone resistance and evaluated proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) as efflux pump-targeting adjuvants. Fifty clinical K. pneumoniae isolates were characterized by antimicrobial susceptibility testing, MDR/XDR classification, phenotypic efflux activity assays, molecular detection of efflux-associated genes, kpnE sequencing, quantitative real-time PCR, molecular docking, and ceftriaxone minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) determination in the presence and absence of omeprazole and lansoprazole. MDR and XDR phenotypes were identified in 70% and 18% of isolates, respectively, whereas active efflux was detected in 14% of isolates and was significantly associated with increasing resistance severity. Sequence analysis demonstrated marked conservation of kpnE, with a single D → G amino acid substitution identified in one isolate. Despite this conservation, gene expression analysis revealed substantial isolate-dependent transcriptional responses that were not directly correlated with phenotypic efflux activity, suggesting that transporter efficiency is governed by complex interactions between transcriptional regulation, structural adaptation, and protein functionality rather than gene expression alone. Molecular docking demonstrated favorable binding of both PPIs to KpnE, KmrA, and KdeA, supporting their potential to interfere with efflux-mediated drug extrusion. Consistent with these predictions, combination assays markedly potentiated ceftriaxone activity, reducing MIC values by up to 16,516-fold and restoring ceftriaxone susceptibility in all seven tested efflux-active ceftriaxone-resistant isolates, with omeprazole producing the greatest synergistic effect. Collectively, these findings provide new mechanistic insight into the role of SMR-associated efflux systems in K. pneumoniae antimicrobial resistance and identify proton pump inhibitors, particularly omeprazole, as potential antibiotic adjuvants for restoring β-lactam efficacy against MDR and XDR K. pneumoniae. Further functional and in vivo studies are warranted to determine whether these in vitro findings can be translated into clinically relevant therapeutic applications.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics, efficacy and safety of dupilumab administered with prefilled pen devices in patients aged <12 years with atopic dermatitis.
articles.abstract: AIM: For children with atopic dermatitis (AD), dupilumab is available as a prefilled syringe (PFS) from the age of 6 months and as a prefilled pen (PFP) for patients aged ≥2 years, in 200- and 300-mg devices. This substudy of an ongoing open-label extension study evaluated the pharmacokinetics, efficacy and safety of switching from a dupilumab PFS device to a PFP device in children aged 2-11 years with AD. METHODS: Patients received 200 mg of dupilumab every 2 weeks (q2w, Cohort 1B) or 300 mg of dupilumab every 4 weeks (q4w, Cohorts 1A and 2B) based on age (2-5 or 6-11 years) and weight (15-<30 or 30-<60 kg). The first dose of the substudy was administered with a PFS, after which patients switched to 12 weeks of treatment with a PFP. Samples for dupilumab concentration included steady-state maximum concentration (Cmax; 4 days post-dose) and steady-state trough concentration (Ctrough; 14 or 28 days post-dose for q2w or q4w), collected after the PFS (reference) and the last PFP (test) doses. RESULTS: Geometric mean ratios (PFP/PFS) of Cmax were 1.019, 0.834 and 0.807 for Cohorts 1A, 1B and 2B, respectively, and 0.896, 1.152 and 0.817 for Ctrough, respectively, indicating a similar drug exposure between PFS and PFP in each cohort. No patients exhibited treatment-emergent antidrug antibody responses after switching to PFP, and dupilumab was well tolerated. CONCLUSION: These results support the use of dupilumab via 200-mg and 300-mg PFP devices for patients aged 2-11 years with AD. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02612454, posted on 23 November 2015.

articles.title: Shengjiang San suppresses C5a/C5aR1-mediated neutrophil activation and NET formation to alleviate acute lung injury.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Excessive neutrophil activation and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation contribute to hyperinflammation and disruption of the alveolar capillary barrier in acute lung injury (ALI). C5a/C5aR1 signaling links complement activation to neutrophil migration, Ca2+ mobilization, ROS production, and NET formation. This study investigated whether Shengjiang San (SJS) regulates these responses in ALI and explored candidate circulating constituents. METHODS: ALI was induced in mice by intratracheal LPS administration, and SJS treatment was initiated before LPS exposure. Lung injury, barrier integrity, neutrophil responses, NET formation, C5a/C5aR1 changes, and lung transcriptomic profiles were assessed. Purified murine neutrophils were stimulated with C5a or PMA to evaluate the effects of SJS-containing serum. Serum pharmacochemistry, plasma exposure analysis, biolayer interferometry, molecular docking, and neutrophil assays were used to characterize ferulic acid. RESULTS: SJS reduced pulmonary inflammation, edema, vascular leakage, neutrophil accumulation and activation, and NET formation, while preserving the integrity of the alveolar capillary barrier. Transcriptomic profiling showed enrichment of complement activation, neutrophil activation, and NET formation among genes differentially expressed between the SJS and Model groups. SJS also lowered C5a concentrations in plasma and lung homogenates and reduced pulmonary C5aR1 expression. In neutrophils, SJS-containing serum significantly suppressed C5a-stimulated neutrophil functions, including migration, Ca2+ flux, oxidative burst, and NET release, while PMX205 produced a similar inhibitory pattern. SJS-containing serum also inhibited PMA-induced NET formation. Ferulic acid was detected in serum as a prototype constituent with measurable plasma exposure, showed concentration-dependent binding to recombinant human C5a with an apparent K D of 21.65 μM, and reduced histone H3 citrullination and NET formation in C5a-stimulated neutrophils. CONCLUSION: SJS attenuated LPS-induced ALI and restrained neutrophil activation and NET formation mediated by C5a/C5aR1 signaling. Ferulic acid was identified as a candidate circulating constituent that reduced C5a-activated NET formation.

articles.title: Unraveling the multitarget mechanisms of aloe emodin against periodontitis: a synergy of network pharmacology and experimental validation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic periodontitis is a prevalent inflammatory disease that leads to destruction of periodontal tissues, resulting in tooth loss. While mechanical debridement and adjunctive antibiotics are commonly used, their therapeutic efficacy is limited by anatomical complexity and concerns over antibiotic resistance and side effects. Aloe-emodin (AE), a naturally occurring anthraquinone compound, exhibits significant anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects. However, its mechanisms in periodontitis remain unclear. METHODS: A network pharmacology approach was employed to identify potential targets of AE in periodontitis. The effects of AE on the viability, proliferation, migration, osteogenic differentiation, and inflammatory responses of mouse periodontal ligament stem cells (mPDLSCs) were assessed CCK8, qPCR and ELISA. In vivo, the alveolar bone of mouse periodontitis model was repaired and evaluated by micro-CT and histological analysis. RESULTS: Network pharmacology analysis identified 179 overlapping targets between AE and periodontitis, with key hubs including TNF, AKT1, EGFR, TP53, and MMP9. These targets were predominantly enriched in the MAPK, PI3K-AKT, NF-κB, and TNF signaling pathways. In vitro, AE significantly enhanced the proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation of mPDLSCs while markedly suppressing LPS-induced expression. In vivo, AE dose-dependently reduced alveolar bone loss, improved trabecular microarchitecture, increased bone mineral density, and enhanced collagen organization in the periodontitis model. CONCLUSION: AE is a pleiotropic natural compound that reprograms the inflammatory-osteolytic microenvironment of periodontitis and promotes alveolar bone regeneration through multi-target pathway modulation.

articles.title: Systemic inflammatory response index: a potential mediator between substance use disorder and sleep disturbance.
articles.abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVES: Substance use disorder (SUD) and sleep disturbance share a complex, bidirectional relationship. However, the role of the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) in this relationship remains to be explored, which will be beneficial for detecting SUD-related sleep disturbances. METHODS: Utilizing diverse samples from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) (n = 2,533) as well as self-collected clinical data (n = 88), we explored the associations among SUD, SIRI, and sleep disturbance. In NHANES dataset, weighted logistic regression and multiple machine learning (ML) models were employed to assess the relationship between SIRI and sleep disturbance, as well as SIRI importance in SUD group. Mediation analysis examined the role of SIRI in mediating the SUD-sleep disturbance association. During clinical confirmation, a two-sample t-test was used to discover differences in SIRI between opioid use disorder (OUD) and healthy controls (HC). Correlation of SIRI and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) was performed by partial correlation within OUD group. RESULTS: The analyses on NHANES datasets uncovered significant "SUD-SIRI-sleep disturbance" relationships, and SIRI ranked first in diagnosing sleep status of SUD subjects. Through validation via clinical datasets, OUD individuals also had higher SIRI levels and sleep disturbance risk than HC. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that SIRI statistically mediates the relationship between SUD and sleep disturbance in a cross-sectional context, positioning it as a potential adjunctive monitoring indicator for SUD-related psychiatric management. These results offer preliminary correlational evidence for mitigating sleep disruption through anti-inflammatory approaches, warranting further longitudinal and experimental validation.

articles.title: Complex antiarrhythmic effects of empagliflozin in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve clinical outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and may reduce sudden cardiac death; however, the underlying antiarrhythmic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We investigated the cellular electrophysiological effects of the SGLT2 inhibitor empagliflozin in isolated cardiomyocytes from two non-ischemic, non-diabetic HFrEF models (rabbit and mouse). RESULTS: Ventricular cardiomyocytes from both HFrEF models exhibited prolonged action potential duration (APD), increased short-term APD variability (STV), and greater susceptibility to APD alternans and delayed afterdepolarizations (DADs). Intracellular Ca2+ buffering with EGTA prevented DADs, attenuated APD prolongation, and reduced repolarization instability. HFrEF cardiomyocytes also showed enhanced late Na+ current (INa,L) and reduced inward rectifier K+ current (IK1). Cell pretreatment with empagliflozin (1 μmol/L, 3 h), but not acute application (3 min), attenuated proarrhythmogenic AP changes, reduced INa,L, and increased IK1 in both species. Empagliflozin had no significant electrophysiological effects in healthy control cardiomyocytes. Selective inhibition of Na+/H+ exchanger-1 (NHE-1) with cariporide (1 μmol/L, 3 h) failed to reproduce the antiarrhythmic effects of empagliflozin under our experimental conditions; however, our studies were performed with intracellular pH buffered to 7.2, where NHE-1 activity is low. DISCUSSION: These results demonstrate that empagliflozin attenuates key proarrhythmic electrophysiological changes in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes. The requirement for drug pretreatment supports the hypothesis that empagliflozin acts through modulation of ion channel functional expression and/or post-translational regulation rather than direct acute channel effects in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes.

articles.title: Sulfated polysaccharide-coated protein nanoparticles for enhanced delivery of psoralen in breast cancer therapy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Psoralen (PSO) is an anticancer agent with a potential role in breast cancer management. Its clinical application, however, is significantly limited by poor aqueous solubility and low bioavailability. Therefore, the development of advanced PSO delivery systems is essential to enhance its therapeutic potential. METHODS: In this study, a novel nano-delivery platform was constructed by encapsulating PSO into zein nanoparticles (NPs) followed by surface modification with fucoidan (Fu), yielding PSO-Z/F NPs. RESULTS: Successful surface modification was confirmed by a reversal in ζ potential from positive values to -24.8 ± 0.02 mV, an increase in particle size to 129.23 ± 0.18 nm, characteristic changes in sulfate-related Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) bands, and the appearance of an S 2p signal in X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The PSO-Z/F NPs exhibited a uniform spherical morphology, with an encapsulation efficiency of 73.13 ± 0.98% and a drug-loading capacity of 5.40 ± 0.35%. Cellular uptake of PSO-Z/F NPs was 1.6-fold higher than that of uncoated PSO-Z NPs (P < 0.05). In vitro, PSO-Z/F NPs significantly suppressed the proliferation, migration, and invasion of 4T1 breast cancer cells. Specifically, wound closure rate decreased from 29.13 ± 3.33 % in the control group to 5.02 ± 2.86% (P < 0.001). Compared with the PSO group, the number of migrated cells decreased from 220 ± 33 to 146 ± 20 (P < 0.01), while that of invaded cells decreased from 144 ± 21 to 90 ± 8 (P < 0.05). Moreover, PSO-Z/F NPs increased the total apoptosis rate from 6.45% in the control group to 17.98% (P < 0.01). In addition, hemolysis assays showed reduced hemolytic activity, while serum-incubation studies confirmed improved colloidal stability, as evidenced by minimal changes in particle size and PDI over 7 days. Notably, in vivo and ex vivo fluorescence analysis of tumors and major organs in 4T1 tumor-bearing mice showed efficient tumor accumulation of PSO-Z/F NPs, and pharmacodynamic studies indicated enhanced tumor growth inhibition with an acceptable biosafety profile. DISCUSSION: Overall, PSO-Z/F NPs may provide a potential nanoparticle-based delivery strategy for improving the therapeutic application of psoralen in breast cancer.

articles.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface. METHODS: Shared disease-associated genes were identified using integrated bioinformatics and protein-protein interaction network analysis, followed by analyses of TCGA and single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Deep learning-based (DeepPurpose) and structure-based (AutoDock Vina) virtual screening were used to prioritize multi-target ligands. Binding was assessed by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and molecular dynamics simulations. Cellular effects were evaluated in a diabetic-mimetic model using high glucose, insulin, and palmitic acid (three factors; TF), with HCT116 cells and THP-1-derived macrophages. RESULTS: The IL1β-CXCL8-CXCR2 axis was prioritized as a candidate inflammatory module at the diabetes-CRC interface. TCGA and single-cell RNA-seq analyses associated axis-related expression with immune infiltration and macrophage polarization-related transcriptional signatures; higher axis expression was also associated with longer overall survival. Hupehenine (HU), a steroidal alkaloid, was identified as a multi-target ligand engaging IL1β, CXCL8, and CXCR2. SPR showed concentration-dependent binding (KD: CXCR2, 505 nM; CXCL8, 2.2 μM; IL1β, 12.7 μM) and interference with CXCL8-CXCR2 binding. In a diabetic-mimetic model, HU reduced HCT116 cell viability, migration, and invasion. TF-conditioned cells were more sensitive to HU than non-TF cells, whereas a corresponding increase in sensitivity was not observed for 5-fluorouracil or oxaliplatin. HU also decreased M2-associated and increased M1-associated macrophage markers. CONCLUSION: These findings support the IL1β-CXCL8-CXCR2 axis as a candidate immunomodulatory module at the diabetes-CRC interface and identify HU as an in vitro multi-target ligand. The observed changes in macrophage markers and differential sensitivity under diabetic-mimetic conditions warrant further mechanistic and preclinical evaluation, including direct assessment of macrophage function.

articles.title: The relationship of homocysteine and its redox forms with renal toxicity after high-dose methotrexate treatment in patients with leukemia or lymphoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: High-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX) chemotherapy inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, leading to impaired homocysteine metabolism, elevated levels, and associated clinical adverse reactions. Currently, studies often monitor total homocysteine (tHcy) levels, but its toxic mechanism remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: Given the association between HD-MTX toxicity and oxidative stress, this study aimed to analyze the correlations between tHcy and its redox forms with liver/kidney function indicators, and to evaluate their discriminatory ability for hepatic and renal toxicity. METHODS: A total of 310 blood samples were collected from 89 patients (38 adults, 51 children) with leukemia or lymphoma treated with HD-MTX. Concentrations of tHcy, free reduced homocysteine (Hcy), free oxidized homocysteine (HHcy, homocystine), and the ratio of Hcy concentration to HHcy concentration (Hcy/HHcy) were measured at 42, 72, and 96 h post-chemotherapy. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to assess associations between tHcy-related redox forms and liver/kidney function indicators, and to compare concentration differences between toxicity and non-toxicity groups. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was applied to evaluate the discriminatory ability of relevant indicators for HD-MTX-related toxicity. RESULTS: In pediatric patients, Hcy/HHcy was significantly negatively correlated with creatinine (CR) (P < 0.028), and tHcy was significantly negatively correlated with alanine aminotransferase (ALT), total bilirubin (TB), and direct bilirubin (DB). No significant associations were observed in adult patients. Compared with the control group, the kidney injury group showed significant differences in Hcy and HHcy levels at 42 h (P < 0.05), Hcy at 72 h, and HHcy at 96 h. No significant differences were observed in the liver injury group. HHcy, tHcy, and Hcy/HHcy at 42 h all demonstrated good discriminatory ability for kidney injury, with HHcy showing an AUC of 0.817 (95% CI: 0.702-0.932, P < 0.01). tHcy at 72 h and 96 h showed reverse discriminatory ability for liver and kidney injury. CONCLUSION: Alterations in tHcy redox status after HD-MTX treatment, particularly changes in HHcy levels and the Hcy/HHcy, may be associated with renal function changes and may have potential value for identifying patients with HD-MTX-related nephrotoxicity.

articles.title: Persistent sarcopenia after flare remission in experimental RA responds to dipyridamole and is associated with restoration of adenosine and A2BR signaling.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with systemic inflammation and sarcopenia, which often persist despite successful control of joint swelling and the mechanisms sustaining it remain unclear. METHODS: Using the K/BxN serum-transfer model, we evaluated muscle structure, metabolism, and function after inflammatory remission. Dipyridamole was administered after remission of joint swelling to assess whether enhancement of adenosine and adenosine receptor signaling restore muscle homeostasis. Histological, molecular, metabolic, and functional analyses were performed. RESULTS: RA mice exhibited persistent loss of muscle mass, fiber atrophy, fibrosis, white adipose tissue expansion, and impaired strength and endurance despite normalization of joint swelling. RA muscle showed sustained myostatin (MSTN) elevation, Akt/mTOR suppression, impaired regeneration, senescence markers, and disrupted purinergic signaling characterized by reduced adenosine levels, diminished adenosine A2B receptor (A2BR) expression, and decreased AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation. Dipyridamole administered after remission of joint swelling restored muscle adenosine availability, reactivated A2BR-AMPK signaling, suppressed MSTN, stimulated insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF1R)-dependent anabolic pathways, reduced fibrosis, and improved muscle function and fiber composition. CONCLUSION: RA induces persistent sarcopenia that remains after inflammation resolution. Post-remission dipyridamole reverses this phenotype in association with restoration of adenosine signaling, increased A2BR expression, AMPK activation, and enhanced anabolic pathways, highlighting purinergic modulation as a promising therapeutic strategy to improve muscle integrity and function in RA remission.

articles.title: Efficacy and durability of GB10, a novel bispecific VEGF/Ang-2 neutralizing fusion protein, in ocular neovascularization models.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the preclinical efficacy, durability, and ocular biodistribution profiling of GB10, a novel bispecific vascular endothelial growth factor/angiopoietin 2 neutralizing fusion protein, compared with faricimab in models of choroidal and retinal neovascularization. METHODS: Cynomolgus monkeys (cyno) with laser-induced choroidal neovascularization (CNV) received intravitreal GB10 (0.07, 0.7, or 7 mg/eye), faricimab (6 mg/eye), or vehicle. Dutch belted rabbits with DL-alpha-aminoadipic acid-induced retinal neovascularization (RNV) received GB10, faricimab, or vehicle. Chinchilla rabbits were used for biodistribution. Efficacy and durability were assessed by fluorescein fundus angiography in cyno CNV model and rabbit RNV model. Tissue concentrations were quantified by ELISA. RESULTS: In the CNV model, GB10 at 0.7 mg/eye achieved similar anti-leakage inhibition at a 9-fold lower dose relative to faricimab at 6 mg/eye (grade 4 incidence: 54.17% vs. 76.39% at week 1). By week 2, GB10 (0.7 and 7 mg/eye) achieved 0% incidence of grade 4 leakage, sustained through week 4. In the RNV model, GB10 sustained inhibitory activity for ≥12 weeks, whereas faricimab showed effects up to 4 weeks for FFA score and 8 weeks for grade 4 leakage. GB10 demonstrated high distribution in retina/choroid (≈35% of total exposure) and minimal systemic exposure (serum proportion 0.02%). CONCLUSION: In preclinical ocular neovascularization models, GB10 shows desirable efficacy at a 9-fold lower dose versus faricimab in cyno CNV model, alongside extended durability of ≥12 weeks (faricimab: 4 weeks for FFA score and 8 weeks for grade 4 leakage area) in rabbit RNV model. These preclinical findings demonstrate GB10's encouraging prospects as a next-generation therapeutic candidate, with efficacy profiles to be confirmed in clinical investigations.

articles.title: Therapeutic effects and mechanisms of neutrophil membrane-coated MXene (Ti 3 C 2 T x ) nanoparticles for sepsis treatment.
articles.abstract: Sepsis, a life-threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated infection response, remains a high-mortality global health burden characterized by the systemic overproduction of pro-inflammatory mediators and reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. Timely anti-infective/anti-inflammatory interventions in the early onset window drastically improve sepsis prognosis, yet current therapeutic efficacy remains severely constrained by the global antibiotic resistance crisis. As a two-dimensional nanomaterial, Ti3C2Tx MXene displays potent intrinsic antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities. We herein engineer a neutrophil membrane-coated Ti3C2Tx nanoplatform (NM@Ti3C2Tx NPs) for targeted sepsis therapy. Experimental validation confirms this formulation mitigates sepsis-triggered oxidative stress injury via synergistic antioxidant pathways, with favorable colloidal stability and confirmed in vitro biocompatibility. In CLP-induced murine sepsis models, it attenuates systemic pro-inflammatory cascades, alleviates hypothermia and multi-organ damage, and improves survival. Collectively, this multifunctional platform integrating targeted antibacterial action and oxidative stress modulation presents a promising candidate for sepsis translational therapy.

articles.title: Exploration of various administration routes for the nitric oxide donating organic nitrite, nitrosooxypropanol, in a porcine model.
articles.abstract: Organic nitrites are restricted to intravenous or inhaled administration. The aim was to explore novel administration routes for an organic nitrite, previously demonstrated to have pulmonary selectivity, in normal and elevated pulmonary vascular resistance. Hemodynamic and respiratory variables, including fraction of exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), were measured in 13 anesthetized pigs. In naïve conditions, nitrosooxypropanol (PDNO) was given subcutaneously (100-1600 nmol/kg/min; 5 min/dose, 30 min interval), intramuscularly (50-400 nmol/kg/min; 5 min/dose, 30 min interval), intravenously (5-80 nmol/kg/min; 30 min infusion), intranasally (500-2000 nmol/kg boli), and sublingually (80-16,240 nmol/kg boli). In pulmonary hypertension (intravenous infusion of U46619), PDNO was given intravenously (5-45 nmol/kg/min; 15-20 mins infusion/dose) and subcutaneously (200-1800 nmol/kg/min; 5 min/dose at 20 min interval). Recovery was calculated using FeNO. PDNO, given by all administration routes, dose-dependently decreased systemic blood pressure and increased FeNO. Subcutaneous and intramuscular administration induced slow-onset (9 min to maximum effect) and long-lasting effects (~30 min). Intravenous administration induced rapid effects (1-2 min to steady state) and prompt decline after infusion cessation. The proportion of PDNO reaching exhaled gas (intravenous administration as reference; FeNO-based recovery) was 17% (intramuscularly) and 9% (subcutaneously). In pulmonary hypertension, intravenous and subcutaneous administration decreased the pulmonary/systemic vascular resistance-ratio. In this exploratory proof-of-concept study evaluating novel administration routes for organic nitrites, PDNO demonstrated measurable biological effects and acceptable FeNO-based recovery following intramuscular and subcutaneous administration. Furthermore, intranasal and tentatively sublingual administration showed biological effects. Future work on formulation and investigations into relevant disease models is warranted.

articles.title: Hepa-SENS: ASGPR-mediated hepatocyte delivery and attenuated unwanted immune recognition for nucleic acid therapeutics.
articles.abstract: An optimal nucleic acid delivery system for hepatic therapeutics should demonstrate consistent pharmacological performance across both normal and diseased hepatic microenvironments, enabling repeated administration with favorable safety profiles. Given the disease-sensitive and relatively low expression of low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) on hepatocytes and compared to the abundant and disease-resilient expression of asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR), ASGPR-mediated drug delivery presents a compelling strategy for liver diseases. Here, we introduce Hepa-SENS, a next-generation polymer-lipid hybrid nanoparticle platform enabling robust ASGPR-mediated hepatocyte delivery without ligand conjugation. Its biodistribution, hepatocyte selectivity, receptor dependence, repeated-dose activity, and therapeutic performance were evaluated in healthy and fibrotic mouse liver models. Hepa-SENS demonstrates strong, hepatocyte-selective transgene expression of mRNA payload preserved under disease conditions, such as high-fatty liver and liver fibrosis, and across multiple species, including non-human primates. In long-term repeat-dose regimens, Hepa-SENS sustained mRNA-driven protein expression without inducing antibodies to the delivery system, enabling greater consistency than conventional lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). In fact, in a liver fibrosis mouse model, where a reduction of LDLR is observed as fibrosis develops, Hepa-SENS outperformed conventional LNPs in delivering therapeutic hepatocyte nuclear factor 4 alpha mRNA and attenuating disease progression. In conclusion, Hepa-SENS represents a robust and versatile delivery platform for nucleic acid therapeutics targeting hepatocytes under disease-relevant conditions via ASGPR-dependent mechanisms. Its repeated-dosing-compatible design supports durable treatment strategies for chronic liver diseases.

articles.title: Drug-Drug Interactions of Cenobamate With Medications: Dose-Dependent Induction/Inhibition and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: Cenobamate causes dose-dependent cytochrome P450 (CYP)2B6 and CYP3A4 induction and CYP2C19 inhibition, raising concern over multi-pathway drug-drug interactions (DDIs) in patients with epilepsy treated with cardiovascular co-medications. We developed a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model for cenobamate and verified it using reported DDIs for cenobamate 200 mg using three probe substrates: bupropion (CYP2B6), midazolam (CYP3A4), and omeprazole (CYP2C19). The verified model predicted exposure changes (area under the curve ratio [AUCR] and maximum concentration [Cmax] ratio with/without cenobamate) for eight drugs, including anticoagulants and antiplatelets (apixaban, cilostazol, clopidogrel, and rivaroxaban), and antihypertensives (amlodipine, bisoprolol, carvedilol, and nifedipine). Regarding anticoagulants and antiplatelets, for apixaban, AUCR/Cmax ratios were 0.78/0.92 (100 mg), 0.71/0.87 (200 mg), and 0.63/0.83 (400 mg), respectively. For cilostazol, parent exposure decreased (0.67/0.85, 0.55/0.77, 0.45/0.70), while the active metabolite OPC-13015 was predicted to increase in Cmax. For clopidogrel, parent exposure was unchanged, but formation of 2-oxo-clopidogrel and clopidogrel-H4 were decreased and increased, respectively. For rivaroxaban, the AUCR/Cmax ratios were 0.78/0.90, 0.69/0.85, and 0.61/0.80. Among antihypertensives, amlodipine showed decreased AUCR/Cmax ratios (0.57/0.66, 0.45/0.55, 0.37/0.47). The exposure changes of bisoprolol were minor (AUCR 0.84-0.92, Cmax ratio 0.95-0.98); AUCR/Cmax ratios of carvedilol fell to 0.73/0.80, 0.63/0.71, and 0.55/0.64; and nifedipine decreased markedly (0.41/0.54, 0.29/0.41, 0.21/0.32). In conclusion, cenobamate induced CYP2B6 weakly and CYP3A4 moderately, and it inhibited CYP2C19 moderately to drive dose-dependent decreases in exposure for seven of eight drugs with minimal change for bisoprolol. The verified PBPK framework enables risk assessment in scenarios not yet clinically tested.

articles.title: Why Lithium Toxicological Reference Values Are Needed for the General Population and Workers?
articles.abstract: Lithium industry can generate a risk of airborne transport of substances, followed by a significant risk of deposition on soils and in water. It raises concerns about chronic low-dose exposure in the general population and occupational exposure among workers. Lithium exposure induces chronic toxicities on kidney, thyroid, heart, and effects on phosphate-calcium metabolism, reproduction and development. Current toxicological knowledge is largely derived from clinical data in patients under lithium treatment, but there is a critical lack of information on health effects associated with environmental exposure levels and on occupational exposures. The establishment of human biomonitoring guidance values (HBM-GVs) allows to aggregate all exposure routes for risk characterization related to real-life exposure. In 2026, the French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health & Safety (ANSES) together with the European Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals (PARC) derived HBM-GVs in serum/plasma of 0.035 mg Li+.L-1 for the general population and 0.10 mg Li+.L-1 for workers, based on adverse effects observed at the minimum therapeutic lithium serum/plasma level of 0.5 mmol.L-1. ANSES also established a long-term oral toxicological reference value of 0.02 mg Li+.kg bw-1.day-1. These values apply to lithium as element and all its inorganic compounds. These guidance values will allow the implementation of management measures.

articles.title: The prognostic impact of cardioselectivity of beta-blockers prescribed during hospitalization for decompensated heart failure.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Beta-blockers (BBs) show considerable variation in cardioselectivity (i.e., the relative affinity to the β1 receptor), even among those with evidence of benefit in the treatment of chronic heart failure (HF). We aimed to evaluate whether the cardioselectivity of BBs prescribed during hospitalization for decompensated HF will affect the long-term prognosis of patients. METHODS: In the prospective study, we followed 4053 patients hospitalized for decompensated HF. The entire cohort was divided into subgroups based on the cardioselectivity of recommended BBs (as stated in discharge summary). RESULTS: After complex adjustment, patients treated with a highly selective BB (bisoprolol) showed significantly lower five-year cardiovascular mortality than those with a lesser degree of cardioselectivity (mainly metoprolol) [hazard ratio (HR) 0.69 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.52-0.92), p = 0.011]. This difference remained in patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) [HR 0.58 (95% CI: 0.37-0.89), p = 0.013], but was not yet significant in HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) [HR 0.66 (95% CI: 0.43-1.02), p = 0.063]. In HFrEF patients only, highly cardioselective BBs also showed a lower risk of cardiovascular mortality than nonselective BBs with vasodilatory properties (mainly carvedilol) [HR 0.55 (95% CI: 0.33-0.93), p = 0.025]. CONCLUSION: The choice of a BB regarding the degree of its cardioselectivity may have a prognostic impact in chronic HF patients.

articles.title: Humidity-Controlled Inverse Gas Chromatography for Characterizing the Adsorption-Relevant Surface State of Dehydration-Sensitive Pharmaceutical Hydrates.
articles.abstract: Preservation of the adsorption-relevant surface state is important for surface characterization of dehydration-sensitive pharmaceutical hydrates because hydration and surface structure may change during sample preparation and measurement. Humidity-controlled inverse gas chromatography (IGC) can prevent bulk hydrate-to-anhydrate transformation during specific surface area measurement; however, preservation of the bulk crystalline phase does not necessarily ensure preservation of the adsorption-relevant surface state. In this study, humidity-controlled IGC was investigated for characterizing the probe-accessible surface area of three pharmaceutical hydrate systems: sodium saccharin dihydrate, L-cysteine hydrochloride monohydrate, and citric acid monohydrate. Hydration behavior was characterized by dynamic vapor sorption, IGC measurements were performed under controlled relative humidity using n-nonane as an adsorption probe, and BET analysis was used to estimate the probe-accessible surface area. Measurements of the certified reference material BCR-170 supported the approach. Under humidity conditions selected based on DVS measurements, adsorption isotherms suitable for BET analysis were obtained for all three hydrate systems, and no detectable morphological changes were observed during the IGC measurement timescale. Importantly, the probe-accessible surface area depended on sample history and elapsed time even under humidity conditions selected to minimize dehydration. In L-cysteine hydrochloride monohydrate, the surface area decreased from 0.43 to 0.30 m2 g⁻1 after 1 day using the same packed column, accompanied by a substantial decrease in pressure drop. These findings indicate that maintaining the hydration environment does not necessarily ensure a time-invariant adsorption-relevant surface state. Humidity-controlled IGC provides an approach for characterizing the surface behavior of dehydration-sensitive pharmaceutical hydrates while minimizing dehydration-related perturbation during measurement.

Design, Synthesis, and CETP Inhibitory Evaluation of Novel P-methoxybenzene Sulfonamides Supported by Molecular Modeling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperlipidemia is a global health concern characterized by elevated blood lipid concentrations, including cholesterol and triglycerides. Cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) plays a crucial role in transferring cholesteryl esters and phospholipids from antiatherogenic high-density lipoproteins to atherogenic low-density and very-low-density lipoproteins. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to synthesize and evaluate 20 p-methoxy-substituted benzene sulfonamides (6a-6j and 7a-7j) as potential CETP inhibitors. METHODS: The compounds were synthesized and structurally characterized using infrared (IR) spectroscopy, carbon-13 nuclear magnetic resonance (13C-NMR) spectroscopy, proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR) spectroscopy, and high-resolution mass spectrometry, followed by evaluation of CETP inhibitory activity. Molecular modeling studies were also performed. RESULTS: The biological assay showed that inhibitors 7f-7j exhibited the highest inhibitory activity, achieving 100% inhibition at 10 µM; inhibitor 7j had an IC50 of 0.55 µM. Compounds 6a-6j and 7a-7e showed CETP inhibition of up to 95%. The presence of an additional ring markedly enhanced activity, likely due to the hydrophobic nature of CETP. The docking results supported this finding, indicating that ligand/4EWS complex formation was driven by hydrophobic interactions and hydrogen-bond formation with the amino acid residues H232 and R201. Higher binding scores were observed for series 7a-7j than for series 6a-6j, highlighting the importance of introducing an additional ring to enhance CETP inhibition. Furthermore, pharmacophore mapping confirmed that these analogues matched the fingerprint of active CETP inhibitors. CONCLUSIONS: A series of novel p-methoxybenzene sulfonamides was synthesized and evaluated as CETP inhibitors.
